Efforts have been dedicated to improving text generation systems by changing the order of training samples in a process known as curriculum learning . Past research on sequence-to-sequence learning showed that curriculum learning helps to improve both the performance and convergence speed.

title: Ownership Verification of DNN Architectures via Hardware Cache Side Channels
creator: Xiaoxuan Lou, Shangwei Guo, Jiwei Li, Tianwei Zhang
description: Abstract Deep Neural Networks (DNN) are gaining higher commercial values in computer vision applications, e.g., image classification, video analytics, etc. This calls for urgent demands of the intellectual property (IP) protection of DNN models. In this paper, we present a novel watermarking scheme to achieve the ownership verification of DNN architectures.

title: Neural Data-to-Text Generation with LM-based Text Augmentation
creator: †Ernie Chang, ⊙ \odot Xiaoyu Shen, †Dawei Zhu, †Vera Demberg, ⊗ \otimes Hui Su
description: Abstract For many new application domains for data-to-text generation, the main obstacle in training neural models consists of a lack of training data. While usually large numbers of instances are available on the data side, often only very few text samples are available. To address this problem, we here propose a novel few-shot approach for this setting.

title: Robust discretization and solvers for elliptic optimal control problems with energy regularization
creator: Ulrich Langer, Olaf Steinbach, Huidong Yang
description: Abstract We consider the finite element discretization and the iterative solution of singularly perturbed elliptic reaction-diffusion equations in three-dimensional computational domains. These equations arise from the optimality conditions for elliptic distributed optimal control problems with energy regularization that were recently studied by M. Neumüller and O. Steinbach (2020).

title: Effective field theory approach to lepton number violating
creator: τ
description: Abstract We continue our endeavor to investigate lepton number violating (LNV) processes at low energies in the framework of effective field theory (EFT). In this work we study the LNV tau decays \tau^{+}\rightarrow\ell^{-}P_{i}^{+}P_{j}^{+} , where \ell=e,~\mu and P^{+}_{i,j} denote the lowest-lying charged pseudoscalars \pi^{+},~K^{+} .

title: Fibration structure for Gromov h-principle
creator: Koji Yamazaki
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Koji Yamazaki. The h-principle is a powerful tool for obtaining solutions to partial differential inequalities and partial differential equations. Gromov discovered the h-principle for the general partial differential relations to generalize the results of Hirsch and Smale. In his book, Gromov generalizes his theorem and discusses the sheaf theoretic h-principle , in which an object called a flexible sheaf plays an important role. We show that a flexible sheaf can be interpreted as a fibrant object with respect to a model structure.

title: Identification of EEG Dynamics during Freezing of Gait and Voluntary Stopping in Patients with Parkinson’s Disease
creator: Zehong Cao, Alka Rachel John, Hsiang-Ting Chen, Kaylena Ehgoetz Martens, Matthew Georgiades, Moran Gilat, Hung T. Nguyen, Simon J. G. Lewis *, and Chin-Teng Lin *
description: Abstract Mobility is severely impacted in patients with Parkinson’s disease (PD), especially when they experience involuntary stopping from the freezing of gait (FOG). Understanding the neurophysiological difference between “voluntary stopping” and “involuntary stopping” caused by FOG is vital for the detection and potential intervention of FOG in the daily lives of patients.

title: Quantum Finite Volume Method for Computational Fluid Dynamics with Classical Input and Output
creator: Zhao-Yun Chen, Cheng Xue, Si-Ming Chen, Bing-Han Lu, Yu-Chun Wu, Ju-Chun Ding, Sheng-Hong Huang, Guo-Ping Guo
description: Abstract Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is a branch of fluid mechanics that uses numerical methods to solve fluid flows. The finite volume method (FVM) is an important one. In FVM, space is discretized to many grid cells. When the number of grid cells grows, massive computing resources are needed correspondingly.

title: Online Statistical Inference for Stochastic Optimization via Kiefer-Wolfowitz Methods
creator: Xi Chen Zehua Lai He Li Yichen Zhang
description: Abstract This paper investigates the problem of online statistical inference of model parameters in stochastic optimization problems via the Kiefer-Wolfowitz algorithm with random search directions. We first present the asymptotic distribution for the Polyak-Ruppert-averaging type Kiefer-Wolfowitz (AKW) estimators, whose asymptotic covariance matrices depend on the distribution of search directions and the function-value query complexity.

title: Structural and Electrical Properties of Bilayer SiX (X= N, P, As and Sb)
creator: Nayereh Ghobadi, Shoeib Babaee Touski
description: Abstract In this work, the structural, electrical, and optical properties of bilayer SiX (X= N, P, As, and Sb) are studied using density functional theory (DFT). Five different stacking orders are considered for every compound and their structural properties are presented. The band structure of these materials demonstrates that they are indirect semiconductors.

title: Collective formation of misfit dislocations at the critical thickness for equilibrium nanowire heterostructures
creator: Thue Christian Thann, Tobias Særkjær †, Sergej Schuwalow, Peter Krogstrup †
description: Abstract In this work we model the evolution of strain energy during different growth stages of heterostructure nanowires. We find that the minimum energy configuration changes abruptly from fully elastically strained to partially relaxed due to collective formation of a misfit dislocation network. The transition at the critical thickness is associated with a characteristic density of misfits.

title: Two-dimensionally stable self-organization arises in simple schooling swimmers through hydrodynamic interactions
creator: Pedro C. Ormonde, Melike Kurt, Amin Mivehchi, Keith W. Moored
description: Abstract We present new constrained and free-swimming experiments and simulations of a pair of pitching hydrofoils interacting in a minimal school. The hydrofoils have an out-of-phase synchronization and they are varied through in-line, staggered, and side-by-side formations within the two-dimensional interaction plane. It is discovered that there is a two-dimensionally stable equilibrium point for a side-by-side formation.

title: A LP relaxation based matheuristic for multi-objective integer programming
creator: Duleabom An 1 , Sophie N. Parragh 1 ,Markus Sinnl 1 and Fabien Tricoire 2 1 Institute of Production and Logistics Management, Johannes Kepler University Linz, Altenberger Straße 69, 4040 Linz, Austria 2 Institute for Transport and Logistics Management, Vienna University of Economics and Business, We
description: Abstract Motivated by the success of matheuristics in the single-objective domain, we propose a very simple linear programming-based matheuristic for three-objective binary integer programming. To tackle the problem, we obtain lower bound sets by means of the vector linear programming solver Bensolve .

title: Localizing Unsynchronized Sensors with Unknown Sources
creator: Dalia El Badawy, Viktor Larsson, Marc Pollefeys, Ivan Dokmanić
description: Abstract We propose a method for sensor array self-localization using a set of sources at unknown locations. The sources produce signals whose times of arrival are registered at the sensors. We look at the general case where neither the emission times of the sources nor the reference time frames of the receivers are known.

title: Does He Wink or Does He Nod? A Challenging Benchmark for Evaluating Word Understanding of Language Models
creator: Lutfi Kerem Senel and Hinrich Schütze
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Lutfi Kerem Senel and Hinrich Schütze. Recent progress in pretraining language models on large corpora has resulted in large performance gains on many NLP tasks. These large models acquire linguistic knowledge during pretraining, which helps to improve performance on downstream tasks via fine-tuning. To assess what kind of knowledge is acquired, language models are commonly probed by querying them with ‘fill in the blank’ style cloze questions. Existing probing datasets mainly focus on knowledge about relations between words and entities.

title: Smooth extensions for inertial manifolds of semilinear parabolic equations Thanks: This work is partially supported by the RSF grant 19-71-30004 as well as the EPSRC grant EP/P024920/1. The authors also would like to thank Dmitry Turaev for many fruitful discussions.
creator: Anna Kostianko and Sergey Zelik 1,2
description: Abstract . The paper is devoted to a comprehensive study of smoothness of inertial manifolds for abstract semilinear parabolic problems. It is well known that in general we cannot expect more than C 1 , ε C^{1,\varepsilon} -regularity for such manifolds (for some positive, but small ε \varepsilon ).

title: An Autonomous Negotiating Agent Framework with Reinforcement Learning Based Strategies and Adaptive Strategy Switching Mechanism Conference: Proc. of the 20th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2021); May 3–7, 2021; Online 356
creator: Ayan Sengupta, Yasser Mohammad, Shinji Nakadai
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ayan Sengupta, Yasser Mohammad, Shinji Nakadai. Despite abundant negotiation strategies in literature, the complexity of automated negotiation forbids a single strategy from being dominant against all others in different negotiation scenarios. To overcome this, one approach is to use mixture of experts, but at the same time one problem of this method is the selection of experts, as this approach is limited by the competency of the experts selected.

title: Scheduling Plans of Tasks Internship report. Supervisors: Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni, Safia-Kedad Sidhoum
creator: Davide Andrea Guastella
description: Abstract We present a heuristic algorithm for solving the problem of scheduling plans of tasks. The plans are ordered vectors of tasks, and tasks are basic operations carried out by resources. Plans are tied by temporal, precedence and resource constraints that makes the scheduling problem hard to solve in polynomial time.

title: On quasi-similarity of multiplication operator on the weighted Bergman space in the unit ball Thanks: ∗ Corresponding author.
creator: Cui Chen ∗ , Ya Wang and Yu-Xia Liang
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Cui Chen ∗ , Ya Wang and Yu-Xia Liang. For α > − 1 \alpha>-1 , let A α 2 ​ ( 𝔹 N ) A_{\alpha}^{2}(\mathbb{B}_{N}) be the weighted Bergman space on the unit ball 𝔹 N \mathbb{B}_{N} in ℂ N \mathbb{C}^{N} .

title: Inhomogeneous activity enhances density phase separation in active model B
creator: Ajeya Krishna, Shradha Mishra
description: Abstract I Abstract We study the binary phase separation in active model B, on a two-dimensional substrate with inhomogeneous activity. Activity was introduced with a maximum value at the center of the box and spread as a Bivariate-Gaussian distribution as we move away from the center. The system was studied for three different intensities of the distribution.

title: Affinoid Dixmier Modules and the deformed Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence
creator: Adam Jones
description: Abstract The affinoid envelope U ⁡ ( ℒ ) ^ K \widehat{U(\mathcal{L})}_{K} of a free, finitely generated ℤ p \mathbb{Z}_{p} -Lie algebra ℒ \mathcal{L} , has proven to be useful within the representation theory of compact p p -adic Lie groups.

title: Absolute Time Calibration of LAXPC aboard AstroSat
creator: Avishek Basu 1,3, Dipankar Bhattacharya 2 and Bhal Chandra Joshi 3
description: Abstract The AstroSat mission carries several high-energy detectors meant for fast timing studies of cosmic sources. In order to carry out high precision multi-wavelength timing studies, it is essential to calibrate the absolute time stamps of these instruments to the best possible accuracy.

title: Study of C C parity violating and strangeness changing J / ψ J/{\psi} → {\to} P ​ P PP weak decays
creator: Yueling Yang, Junliang Lu, Mingfei Duan, Jinshu Huang, Junfeng Sun
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yueling Yang, Junliang Lu, Mingfei Duan, Jinshu Huang, Junfeng Sun. Although J / ψ J/{\psi} weak decays are rare, they are possible within the standard model of elementary particles. Inspired by the potential prospects of the future intensity frontier, the C C parity violating J / ψ J/{\psi} → {\to} π η ( ′ ) {\pi}{\eta}^{({\prime})} , η ​ η ′ {\eta}{\eta}^{\prime} decays and the strangeness changing J / ψ J/{\psi} → {\to} π ​ K {\pi}K , K η ( ′ ) K{\eta}^{({\prime})}

title: Gated3D: Monocular 3D Object Detection From Temporal Illumination Cues
creator: Frank Julca-Aguilar Jason Taylor Mario Bijelic Fahim Mannan Ethan Tseng Felix Heide
description: Abstract Today’s state-of-the-art methods for 3D object detection are based on lidar, stereo, or monocular cameras. Lidar-based methods achieve the best accuracy, but have a large footprint, high cost, and mechanically-limited angular sampling rates, resulting in low spatial resolution at long ranges.

title: Symmetry breaking in a turbulent environment
creator: Alexandros Alexakis, Santiago J. Benavides, Kannabiran Seshasayanan, François Pétrélis
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alexandros Alexakis, Santiago J. Benavides, Kannabiran Seshasayanan, François Pétrélis. In this work we investigate symmetry breaking in the presence of a turbulent environment. The transition from a symmetric state to a symmetry-breaking state is demonstrated using two examples: (i) the transition of a two-dimensional flow to a three dimensional flow as the fluid layer thickness is varied and (ii) the dynamo instability in a thin layer flow as the magnetic Reynolds number is varied.

title: Quasinormal modes of charged fermions in linear dilaton black hole spacetime: Exact frequencies DOI: 10.3906/fiz-2012-6
creator: İzzet SAKALLI 1 , Gülnihal TOKGÖZ HYUSEIN 1,2 1 Physics Department, Eastern Mediterranean University, Famagusta, North Cyprus 99628 via Mersin 10, Turkey 2 Güzeloba Mahallesi, Örnekköy Caddesi, Örnekköy Sitesi, 2993 Ada, 11KA Blok, No: 2, Muratpaşa 07230 Antalya, Turkey Corresponding Author: İzzet S
description: Abstract We study charged massless fermionic perturbations in the background of 4 4 -dimensional linear dilaton black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory with double Liouville-type potentials. We present the analytical fermionic quasinormal modes, whose Dirac equations are solved in terms of hypergeometric functions. We also discuss the stability of these black holes under the charged fermionic perturbations.

title: Representation theoretic embedding of twisted Dirac operators Thanks: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification . Primary: 22E46; Secondary: 43A85 Thanks: P. Pandžić was supported by the QuantiXLie Center of Excellence, a project cofinanced by the Croatian Government and European Union through the Eur
creator: S. Mehdi, P. Pandžić
description: Abstract . Let G G be a non-compact connected semisimple real Lie group with finite center. Suppose L L is a non-compact connected closed subgroup of G G acting transitively on a symmetric space G / H G/H such that L ∩ H L\cap H is compact.

title: Halving the width of Toffoli based constant modular addition to n+3 qubits
creator: Oumarou Oumarou, Alexandru Paler, Robert Basmadjian
description: Abstract We present an arithmetic circuit performing constant modular addition having 𝒪 ⁡ ( n ) \mathcal{O}(n) depth of Toffoli gates and using a total of n + 3 n+3 qubits. This is an improvement by a factor of two compared to the width of the state-of-the-art Toffoli-based constant modular adder.

title: COVID-19 and Unemployment Risk: Lessons for the Vaccination Campaign
creator: Valentina Pieroni, Angelo Facchini, Massimo Riccaboni
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Valentina Pieroni, Angelo Facchini, Massimo Riccaboni. Assessing the economic impact of COVID-19 pandemic and public health policies is essential for a rapid recovery. In this paper, we analyze the impact of mobility contraction on furloughed workers and excess deaths in Italy. We provide a link between the reduction of mobility and excess deaths, confirming that the first countrywide lockdown has been effective in curtailing the COVID-19 epidemics.

title: Extremal learning: extremizing the output of a neural network in regression problems
creator: Zakaria Patel, and Markus Rummel
description: Abstract Neural networks allow us to model complex relationships between variables. We show how to efficiently find extrema of a trained neural network in regression problems. Finding the extremizing input of an approximated model is formulated as the training of an additional neural network with a loss function that minimizes when the extremizing input is achieved.

title: Deep Semi-supervised Learning for Time Series Classification
creator: Jann Goschenhofer 1,2 , Rasmus Hvingelby 2 , David Ruegamer 1 , Janek Thomas 1 , Moritz Wagner 2 , Bernd Bischl 1,2
description: Abstract While deep semi-supervised learning has gained much attention in computer vision, limited research exists on its applicability in the time series domain. In this work, we investigate the transferability of state-of-the-art deep semi-supervised models from image to time series classification.

title: High Energy Behaviour of Light Meson Photoproduction
creator: Moskov J. Amaryan, William J. Briscoe, Michael G. Ryskin, Igor I. Strakovsky
description: Abstract We evaluated CLAS Collaboration measurements for the 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} meson photoproduction off the nucleon using a tagged photon beam spanning the energy interval s = 3 − 11 s=3-11 GeV 2 . The results are compared with the ”Quark Counting Rules” predictions.

title: The DKU-Duke-Lenovo System Description for the Third DIHARD Speech Diarization Challenge
creator: 1 st Weiqing Wang, 2 nd Qingjian Lin, 3 rd Danwei Cai, 4 th Lin Yang, 5 th Ming Li
description: Abstract In this paper, we present the submitted system for the third DIHARD Speech Diarization Challenge from the DKU-Duke-Lenovo team. Our system consists of several modules: voice activity detection (VAD), segmentation, speaker embedding extraction, attentive similarity scoring, agglomerative hierarchical clustering. In addition, the target speaker VAD (TSVAD) is used for the phone call data to further improve the performance.

title: A new approach to separation of variables for the Clebsch integrable system. Part II: Inversion of the Abel–Prym map
creator: Y. Fedorov, F. Magri, T. Skrypnyk
description: Abstract This is the second part of a paper describing a new concept of separation of variables applied to the classical Clebsch integrable case. The quadratures obtained in Part I lead to a new type of the Abel map which contains Abelian integrals on two different algebraic curves.

title: Laplace-Beltrami spectrum of ellipsoids that are close to spheres and analytic perturbation theory
creator: Suresh Eswarathasan, Theodore Kolokolnikov
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Suresh Eswarathasan, Theodore Kolokolnikov. We study the spectrum of the Laplace Beltrami operator on ellipsoids. For ellipsoids that are close to the sphere, we use analytic perturbation theory to estimate the eigenvalues up to two orders. We show that for biaxial ellipsoids sufficiently close to the sphere, the first L 2 L^{2} eigenvalues have multiplicity at most two, and characterize those that are simple.

title: On the existence and regularity of solutions of semi-hyperbolic patches to 2-D Euler equations with van der Waals gas
creator: Rahul Barthwal, T. Raja Sekhar
description: Abstract This article is concerned in establishing the existence and regularity of solution of semi-hyperbolic patch problem for two-dimensional isentropic Euler equations with van der Waals gas. This type of solution appears in the transonic flow over an airfoil and Guderley reflection and is very common in the numerical solution of Riemann problems.

title: Symmetry-breaking mechanism for the formation of cluster chimera patterns
creator: Malbor Asllani, Bram A. Siebert, Alex Arenas, James P. Gleeson
description: Abstract The emergence of order in collective dynamics is a fascinating phenomenon that characterizes many natural systems consisting of coupled entities. Synchronization is such an example where individuals, usually represented by either linear or nonlinear oscillators, can spontaneously act coherently with each other when the interactions’ configuration fulfills certain conditions.

title: Nested Group Testing Procedures for Screening
creator: Yaakov Malinovsky and Paul S. Albert
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yaakov Malinovsky and Paul S. Albert. This article reviews a class of adaptive group testing procedures that operate under a probabilistic model assumption as follows. Consider a set of N N items, where item i i has the probability p p ( p i p_{i} in the generalized group testing) to be defective, and the probability 1 − p 1-p to be non-defective independent from the other items.

title: Under the Spotlight: Web Tracking in Indian Partisan News Websites
creator: Vibhor Agarwal ⋆ α {}^{\star}{}^{\alpha} , Yash Vekaria ⋆ α {}^{\star}{}^{\alpha} , Pushkal Agarwal β , Sangeeta Mahapatra γ , Shounak Set β , Sakthi Balan Muthiah α , Nishanth Sastry δ , Nicolas Kourtellis ζ
description: Abstract . India is experiencing intense political partisanship and sectarian divisions. The paper performs, to the best of our knowledge, the first comprehensive analysis on the Indian online news media with respect to tracking and partisanship. We build a dataset of 103 online, mostly mainstream news websites.

title: A bandit approach to curriculum generation for automatic speech recognition
creator: Anastasia Kuznetsova, Anurag Kumar, Francis M. Tyers
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Anastasia Kuznetsova, Anurag Kumar, Francis M. Tyers. The Automated Speech Recognition (ASR) task has been a challenging domain especially for low data scenarios with few audio examples. This is the main problem in training ASR systems on the data from low-resource or marginalized languages. In this paper we present an approach to mitigate the lack of training data by employing Automated Curriculum Learning in combination with an adversarial bandit approach inspired by Reinforcement learning.

title: An empirical comparison and characterisation of nine popular clustering methods
creator: Christian Hennig
description: Abstract Nine popular clustering methods are applied to 42 real data sets. The aim is to give a detailed characterisation of the methods by means of several cluster validation indexes that measure various individual aspects of the resulting clusters such as small within-cluster distances, separation of clusters, closeness to a Gaussian distribution etc. as introduced in Hennig 2019 .

title: Recommending More Efficient Workflows to Software Developers
creator: Dylan Bates
description: Abstract Existing recommendation systems can help developers improve their software development abilities by recommending new programming tools, such as a refactoring tool or a program navigation tool. However, simply recommending tools in isolation may not, in and of itself, allow developers to successfully complete their tasks.

title: COVIDHunter: An Accurate, Flexible, and Environment-Aware Open-Source COVID-19 Outbreak Simulation Model
creator: Mohammed Alser, Jeremie S. Kim, Nour Almadhoun Alserr, Stefan W. Tell, and Onur Mutlu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mohammed Alser, Jeremie S. Kim, Nour Almadhoun Alserr, Stefan W. Tell, and Onur Mutlu. Background: Early detection and isolation of COVID-19 patients are essential for successful implementation of mitigation strategies and eventually curbing the disease spread. With a limited number of daily COVID-19 tests performed in every country, simulating the COVID-19 spread along with the potential effect of each mitigation strategy currently remains one of the most effective ways in managing the healthcare system and guiding policy-makers.

title: Emergency Department Optimization and Load Prediction in Hospitals
creator: Karthik K. Padthe, Vikas Kumar, Carly M. Eckert MD MPH, Nicholas M. Mark MD,, Anam Zahid, Muhammad Aurangzeb Ahmad, Ankur Teredesai,
description: Abstract Over the past several years, across the globe, there has been an increase in people seeking care in emergency departments (EDs). ED resources, including nurse staffing, are strained by such increases in patient volume. Accurate forecasting of incoming patient volume in emergency departments (ED) is crucial for efficient utilization and allocation of ED resources.

title: FastAD: Expression Template-Based C++ Library for Fast and Memory-Efficient Automatic Differentiation
creator: James Yang
description: Abstract Automatic differentiation is a set of techniques to efficiently and accurately compute the derivative of a function represented by a computer program. Existing C++ libraries for automatic differentiation (e.g. Adept, Stan Math Library), however, exhibit large memory consumptions and runtime performance issues.

title: Conformational Biases of α \alpha -synuclein and Formation of Transient Knots
creator: Mateusz Chwastyk, Marek Cieplak
description: Abstract We study local conformational biases in the dynamics of α \alpha -synuclein by using all-atom simulations with explicit and implicit solvents. The biases are related to the frequency of the specific contact formation. In both approaches, the protein is intrinsically disordered and its strongest bias is to make bend, and then turn, local structures.

title: Linking Labs: Interconnecting Experimental Environments
creator: Tanja Schultz
description: Abstract Abstract We introduce the concept of LabLinking : a technology-based interconnection of experimental laboratories across institutions, disciplines, cultures, languages, and time zones - in other words experiments without borders . In particular, we introduce LabLinking levels (LLL), which define the degree of tightness of empirical interconnection between labs.

title: Semi-Automated Creation of Density Functional Tight Binding Models Through Leveraging Chebyshev Polynomial-based Force Fields
creator: Nir Goldman, Kyoung E. Kweon, Babak Sadigh, Tae Wook Heo, Rebecca K. Lindsey, C. Huy Pham, Laurence E. Fried, Bálint Aradi, Kiel Holliday, Jason R. Jeffries, Brandon C. Wood

title: Markovian approximation for Pauli Fierz operators
creator: L. Amour, J. Nourrigat
description: Abstract The purpose of this article is to derive a Markovian approximation of the reduced time dynamics of observables for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian with a precise control of the error terms. In that aim, we define a Lindblad operator associated to the corresponding quantum master equation. In a particular case, this allows to study the transition probability matrix.

title: Understanding Higher-order Structures in Evolving Graphs: A Simplicial Complex based Kernel Estimation Approach
creator: Manohar Kaul and Masaaki Imaizumi
description: Abstract . Dynamic graphs are rife with higher-order interactions, such as co-authorship relationships and protein-protein interactions in biological networks, that naturally arise between more than two nodes at once. In spite of the ubiquitous presence of such higher-order interactions, limited attention has been paid to the higher-order counterpart of the popular pairwise link prediction problem.

title: Dynamic Maximum Entropy provides accurate approximation of structured population dynamics
description: Abstract . Realistic models of biological processes typically involve interacting components on multiple scales, driven by changing environment and inherent stochasticity. Such models are often analytically and numerically intractable. We revisit a dynamic maximum entropy method that combines a static maximum entropy and a quasi-stationary approximation.

title: Non-gaussianities for primordial black hole formation
creator: Marco Taoso a, Alfredo Urbano b,c
description: Abstract We analyze primordial non-gaussianities in presence of an ultra-slow phase during the inflationary dynamics, focusing on scenarios relevant for the production of primordial black holes. We compute the three-point correlation function of comoving curvature perturbations finding that non-gaussianities are sizable, and predominantly local.

title: Hyperbolic Potentials for Continuous Non-Uniformly Expanding Maps
creator: Eduardo Santana
description: Abstract . In this work, we give a class of examples of hyperbolic potentials (including the null one) for continuous non-uniformly expanding maps. It implies the existence and uniqueness of equilibrium state (in particular, of maximal entropy measure). Among the maps considered is the important class known as Viana maps. 1.

title: On the Schmidt and analytic ranks for trilinear forms Thanks: K. A. is supported by ERC grant 716424 - CASe and ISF Grant 1050/16. T. Z. is supported by ERC grant ErgComNum 682150 and ISF grant 2112/20.
creator: Karim Adiprasito, David Kazhdan and Tamar Ziegler
description: Abstract . We discuss relations between different notions of ranks for multilinear forms. In particular we show that the Schmidt and the analytic ranks for trilinear forms are essentially proportional. 1. Introduction In recent years there is growing interest in properties of polynomials which are independent of the number of variables.

title: Superconformal index of low-rank gauge
creator: theories via the Bethe Ansatz
description: Abstract SISSA 07/2021/FISI 1 Introduction and results The AdS/CFT correspondence [ 2 , 3 , 4 ] provides us with a non-perturbative definition of quantum gravity in anti-de-Sitter (AdS) space, in terms of an ordinary quantum field theory (QFT) living on its conformal boundary.

title: Ballistic Transport for Schrödinger Operators with Quasi-periodic Potentials
creator: Yulia Karpeshina, Leonid Parnovski and Roman Shterenberg
description: Abstract . We prove the existence of ballistic transport for a Schrödinger operator with a generic quasi-periodic potential in any dimension d > 1 d>1 . 1. Introduction 1.1. Prior results on ballistic transport It is well known that the spectral and dynamical properties of Schrödinger operators H=-\Delta+V acting in {\mathcal{H}}=L^{2}({\mathbb{R}}^{d}) are related.

title: Mobility-based contact exposure explains the disparity of spread of COVID-19 in urban neighborhoods
creator: Rajat Verma, Takahiro Yabe, Satish V. Ukkusuri
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Rajat Verma, Takahiro Yabe, Satish V. Ukkusuri. The rapid early spread of COVID-19 in the U.S. was experienced very differently by different socioeconomic groups and business industries. In this study, we study aggregate mobility patterns of New York City and Chicago to identify the relationship between the amount of interpersonal contact between people in urban neighborhoods and the disparity in the growth of positive cases among these groups.

title: Fission fragment distributions and their impact on the r-process nucleosynthesis in neutron star mergers
creator: J.-F. Lemaître, S. Goriely, A. Bauswein, H.-T. Janka
description: Abstract Neutron star (NS) merger ejecta offer a viable site for the production of heavy r-process elements with nuclear mass numbers A ≳ 140 A\gtrsim 140 . The crucial role of fission recycling is responsible for the robustness of this site against many astrophysical uncertainties.

title: Phase-modulated Autler-Townes splitting in a giant-atom system within waveguide QED
creator: Wei Zhao, Yan Zhang, Zhihai Wang
description: Abstract The nonlocal emitter-waveguide coupling, which gives birth to the so called giant atom, represents a new paradigm in the field of quantum optics and waveguide QED. In this paper, we investigate the single-photon scattering in a one-dimensional waveguide on a two-level or three-level giant atom.

title: Quasi-free Neutron Knockout Reaction Reveals a Small s s -orbital Component in the Borromean Nucleus 17 B
creator: Z. H. Yang, Y. Kubota, A. Corsi, K. Yoshida, X.-X. Sun, J. G. Li, M. Kimura, N. Michel, K. Ogata, C. X. Yuan, Q. Yuan, G. Authelet, H. Baba, C. Caesar, D. Calvet, A. Delbart, M. Dozono, J. Calvet, A. Delbart, M. Dozono, J. Feng, F. Flavigny, J.-M. Gheller, J. Gibelin, A. Giganon, A. Gillibert, K. Hasegawa, T. Isobe, Y. Kanaya, S. Ka.

title: Search for a D ​ D ¯ D\bar{D} bound state in the Λ b → Λ ​ D ​ D ¯ \Lambda_{b}\rightarrow\Lambda D\bar{D} process
creator: Le-Le Wei, Hong-Shen Li, En Wang, Ju-Jun Xie, De-Min Li, Yu-Xiao Li
description: Abstract We have investigated the process of Λ b → Λ ​ D ​ D ¯ \Lambda_{b}\to\Lambda D\bar{D} , by taking into account the contributions from the s s -wave D ​ D ¯ D\bar{D} interaction within the coupled-channel unitary approach, and the intermediate ψ ⁡ ( 3770 ) \psi(3770) resonance.

title: Efficient Learning of a Linear Dynamical System with Stability Guarantees
creator: Wouter Jongeneel, Tobias Sutter, Daniel Kuhn
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Wouter Jongeneel, Tobias Sutter, Daniel Kuhn. We propose a principled method for projecting an arbitrary square matrix to the non-convex set of asymptotically stable matrices. Leveraging ideas from large deviations theory, we show that this projection is optimal in an information-theoretic sense and that it simply amounts to shifting the initial matrix by an optimal linear quadratic feedback gain, which can be computed exactly and highly efficiently by solving a standard linear quadratic regulator problem.

title: Lifetime-resolved Photon-Correlation Fourier Spectroscopy
creator: Hendrik Utzat, Moungi G. Bawendi
description: Abstract The excited state population of single solid-state emitters is subjected to energy fluctuations around the equilibrium driven by the bath and relaxation through the emission of phonons or photons. Simultaneous measurement of the associated spectral dynamics requires a technique with a high spectral and temporal resolution with an additionally high temporal dynamic range.

title: SiO, 29 SiO, and 30 SiO emission from 67 oxygen-rich stars. A survey of 61 maser lines from 7 to 1 mm Journal: Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series Facilities: MDSCC:DSS-54, IRAM:30m
creator: J. R. Rizzo, J. Cernicharo, C. García-Miró
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J. R. Rizzo, J. Cernicharo, C. García-Miró. Circumstellar environments of oxygen-rich stars are among the strongest SiO maser emitters. Physical processes such as collisions, infrared pumping and overlaps favors the inversion of level population and produce maser emission at different vibrational states. Despite numerous observational and theoretical efforts, we still do not have an unified picture including all the physical processes involved in the SiO maser emission. The aim of this work is to provide homogeneous data in a large sample of oxygen-rich stars.

title: Separability Problems in Creative Telescoping Thanks: S. Chen was partially supported by the NSFC grants 11871067, 11688101, the Fund of the Youth Innovation Promotion Association, CAS, and the National Key Research and Development Project 2020YFA0712300. R. Feng was partially supported by the NSFC
creator: Shaoshi Chen, Ruyong Feng, Pingchuan Ma, Michael F. Singer
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shaoshi Chen, Ruyong Feng, Pingchuan Ma, Michael F. Singer. For given multivariate functions specified by algebraic, differential or difference equations, the separability problem is to decide whether they satisfy linear differential or difference equations in one variable. In this paper, we will explain how separability problems arise naturally in creative telescoping and present some criteria for testing the separability for several classes of special functions, including rational functions, hyperexponential functions, hypergeometric terms, and algebraic functions.

title: Fairness in ERC token markets: A Case Study of CryptoKitties
creator: Kentaro Sako, Shin’ichiro Matsuo, Sachin Meier
description: Abstract Fairness is an important trait of open, free markets. Ethereum is a platform meant to enable digital, decentralized markets. Though many researchers debate the market’s fairness, there are few discussions around the fairness of automated markets, such as those hosted on Ethereum. In this paper, using pilot studies, we consider unfair factors caused by adding the program.

title: On Procrustes Analysis in Hyperbolic Space
creator: Puoya Tabaghi, Ivan Dokmanić
description: Abstract Congruent Procrustes analysis aims to find the best matching between two point sets through rotation, reflection and translation. We formulate the Procrustes problem for hyperbolic spaces, review the canonical definition of the center of point sets, and give a closed form solution for the optimal isometry for noise-free measurements.

title: Adversarial Imaging Pipelines
creator: Buu Phan Algolux, Fahim Mannan Algolux, Felix Heide Algolux, Princeton University
description: Abstract Adversarial attacks play an essential role in understanding deep neural network predictions and improving their robustness. Existing attack methods aim to deceive convolutional neural network (CNN)-based classifiers by manipulating RGB images that are fed directly to the classifiers. However, these approaches typically neglect the influence of the camera optics and image processing pipeline (ISP) that produce the network inputs.

title: Classification based on Topological Data Analysis
creator: Rolando Kindelan, José Frías, Mauricio Cerda, Nancy Hitschfeld
description: Abstract Topological Data Analysis (TDA) is an emergent field that aims to discover topological information hidden in a dataset. TDA tools have been commonly used to create filters and topological descriptors to improve Machine Learning (ML) methods. This paper proposes an algorithm that applies TDA directly to multi-class classification problems, even imbalanced datasets, without any further ML stage.

title: Cwebs beyond three loops in multiparton amplitudes
creator: Neelima Agarwal, Lorenzo Magnea, Sourav Pal, Anurag Tripathi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Neelima Agarwal, Lorenzo Magnea, Sourav Pal, Anurag Tripathi. Correlators of Wilson-line operators in non-abelian gauge theories are known to exponentiate, and their logarithms can be organised in terms of collections of Feynman diagrams called webs . In Agarwal:2020nyc we introduced the concept of Cweb , or correlator web , which is a set of skeleton diagrams built with connected gluon correlators, and we computed the mixing matrices for all Cwebs connecting four or five Wilson lines at four loops.

title: Role of Attentive History Selection in Conversational Information Seeking
creator: Somil Gupta, Neeraj Sharma
description: Abstract . The rise of intelligent assistant systems like Siri and Alexa have led to the emergence of Conversational Search, a research track of Information Retrieval (IR) that involves interactive and iterative information-seeking user-system dialog. Recently released OR-QuAC and TCAsT19 datasets narrow their research focus on the retrieval aspect of conversational search i.e.

title: State-Aware Variational Thompson Sampling for Deep Q-Networks Conference: Proc. of the 20th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2021); May 3–7, 2021; Online 417
creator: Siddharth Aravindan, Wee Sun Lee
description: Abstract . Thompson sampling is a well-known approach for balancing exploration and exploitation in reinforcement learning. It requires the posterior distribution of value-action functions to be maintained; this is generally intractable for tasks that have a high dimensional state-action space.

title: An Analysis of Frame-skipping in Reinforcement Learning Thanks: Equal contribution
creator: Shivaram Kalyanakrishnan, Siddharth Aravindan *, Vishwajeet Bagdawat *, Varun Bhatt *, Harshith Goka *, Archit Gupta *, Kalpesh Krishna *, Vihari Piratla *
description: Abstract . In the practice of sequential decision making, agents are often designed to sense state at regular intervals of d d time steps, d > 1 d>1 , ignoring state information in between sensing steps. While it is clear that this practice can reduce sensing and compute costs, recent results indicate a further benefit.

creator: Jun-Jie Wei, Xue-Feng Wu

title: Curving Origami with Mechanical Frustration
creator: T. Jules 1,2, F. Lechenault 2, M. Adda-Bedia 1
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by T. Jules 1,2, F. Lechenault 2, M. Adda-Bedia 1. We study the three-dimensional equilibrium shape of a shell formed by a deployed accordion-like origami, made from an elastic sheet decorated by a series of parallel creases crossed by a central longitudinal crease. Surprisingly, while the imprinted crease network does not exhibit a geodesic curvature, the emergent structure is characterized by an effective curvature produced by the deformed central fold.

title: PAC-Bayes Bounds for Meta-learning with Data-Dependent Prior
creator: Tianyu Liu, Jie Lu, Zheng Yan, and Guangquan Zhang
description: Abstract By leveraging experience from previous tasks, meta-learning algorithms can achieve effective fast adaptation ability when encountering new tasks. However it is unclear how the generalization property applies to new tasks. Probably approximately correct (PAC) Bayes bound theory provides a theoretical framework to analyze the generalization performance for meta-learning.

title: A symplectic formula of generalized Casson invariants
creator: Shaoyun Bai
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shaoyun Bai. Suppose Y Y is an integer homology 3-sphere, Taubes [ 28 ] proved that the number of irreducible critical orbits of the perturbed Chern-Simons functional on Y Y , counted with signs, is equal to the algebraic intersection number of two character varieties associated with Heegaard splittings when the structure group is SU ⁡ ( 2 ) \SU(2) . Taubes’ result established a relationship between gauge theory and the Casson invariant.

title: Relativistic corrections to decays of heavy baryons in the quark model
creator: Ahmad Jafar Arifi, Daiki Suenaga, Atsushi Hosaka
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ahmad Jafar Arifi, Daiki Suenaga, Atsushi Hosaka. We investigate relativistic corrections of an order 1 / m 2 1/m^{2} , where m m is the constituent quark mass, to heavy baryon decays by emitting one pseudoscalar meson in the quark model. This work is motivated by shortcomings in the previous studies in the nonrelativistic quark model for decays of the Roper-like states such as Λ c ​ ( 2765 ) \Lambda_{c}(2765) .

title: The role of local bond-order at crystallization in a simple supercooled liquid
creator: Søren Toxvaerd
description: Abstract Large scale Molecular Dynamics simulations of sixty-five systems with N N =80000 Lennard-Jones particles at two different supercooled liquid state points reveal, that the supercooled states contain spatially heterogeneous distributed subdomains of particles with significant higher bond-order than the mean bond-order in the supercooled liquid.

title: Frame Codes For Distributed Coded Computation
creator: Royee Yosibash, Royee Yosibash and Ram Zamir
description: Abstract Distributed computation is a framework used to break down a complex computational task into smaller tasks and distributing them among computational nodes. Erasure correction codes have recently been introduced and have become a popular workaround to the well known “straggling nodes” problem, in particular, by matching linear coding for linear computation tasks.

title: Dissipative soliton interaction in Kerr resonators with high-order dispersion
creator: A. G. Vladimirov a , M. Tlidi b , and M. Taki c
description: Abstract We consider an optical resonator containing a photonic crystal fiber and driven coherently by an injected beam. This device is described by a generalized Lugiato-Lefever equation with fourth order dispersion. We use an asymptotic approach to derive interaction equations governing the slow time evolution of the coordinates of two interacting dissipative solitons.

title: Towards establishing an abundant B B and B s B_{s} spectrum up to the second orbital excitations
creator: Qi Li, Ru-Hui Ni, Xian-Hui Zhong
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Qi Li, Ru-Hui Ni, Xian-Hui Zhong. Stimulated by the exciting progress in experiments, we carry out a combined analysis of the masses, and strong and radiative decay properties of the B B and B s B_{s} -meson states up to the second orbital excitations.

title: Robust Explanations for Private Support Vector Machines
creator: Rami Mochaourab, Sugandh Sinha, Stanley Greenstein, Panagiotis Papapetrou
description: Abstract We consider counterfactual explanations for private support vector machines (SVM), where the privacy mechanism that publicly releases the classifier guarantees differential privacy. While privacy preservation is essential when dealing with sensitive data, there is a consequent degradation in the classification accuracy due to the introduced perturbations in the classifier weights.

title: Absolutely Continuous Invariant Measure for Generalized Horseshoe Maps
creator: Abbas Fakhari and Maryam Khalaj
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Abbas Fakhari and Maryam Khalaj. In this paper, we study the SRB measures of generalized horseshoe map. We prove that under the conditions of transversality and fatness, the SRB measure is actually absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure. Introduction The transversality condition was introduced in the 90s to calculate the Hausdorff dimension of the self-similar sets and to find absolutely continuous invariant measures.

title: The Balanced Mode Decomposition Algorithm for Data-Driven LPV Low-Order Models of Aeroservoelastic Systems Journal: Aerospace Science and Technology (AESCTE)
creator: Andrea Iannelli, Urban Fasel, Roy S. Smith
description: Abstract A novel approach to reduced-order modeling of high-dimensional systems with time-varying properties is proposed. It combines the problem formulation of the Dynamic Mode Decomposition method with the concept of balanced realization. It is assumed that the only information available on the system comes from input, state, and output trajectories, thus the approach is fully data-driven.

title: Ripple-like instability in the simulated gel phase of finite size phosphocholine bilayers
creator: Vivien Walter, Céline Ruscher, Adrien Gola, Carlos M. Marques, Olivier Benzerara, Fabrice Thalmann
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Vivien Walter, Céline Ruscher, Adrien Gola, Carlos M. Marques, Olivier Benzerara, Fabrice Thalmann. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations have reached a degree of maturity that makes it possible to investigate the lipid polymorphism of model bilayers over a wide range of temperatures. However if both the fluid L α L_{\alpha} and tilted gel L β ′ L_{\beta^{\prime}} states are routinely obtained, the P β ′ P_{\beta^{\prime}} ripple phase of phosphatidylcholine lipid bilayers is still unsatifactorily described.

title: Coarse selectors of groups
creator: Igor Protasov
description: Abstract . For a group G G , ℱ G \mathcal{F}_{G} denotes the set of all non-empty finite subsets of G G . We extend the finitary coarse structure of G G from G × G G\times G to ℱ G × ℱ G \mathcal{F}_{G}\times\mathcal{F}_{G} and say that a macro-uniform mapping f : ℱ G → ℱ G f:\mathcal{F}_{G}\rightarrow\mathcal{F}_{G} (resp.

title: Global solvability and asymptotical behavior in a two-species chemotaxis model with signal absorption Thanks: ∗ Corresponding author.
creator: Guoqiang Ren, Tian Xiang ∗
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Guoqiang Ren, Tian Xiang ∗. In this work, we study global existence, eventual smoothness and asymptotical behavior of positive solutions for the following two-species chemotaxis consumption model: { u t = Δ u − χ 1 ∇ ⋅ ( u ∇ w ) , x ∈ Ω , t > 0 , v t = Δ v − χ 2 ∇ ⋅ ( u ∇ w ) , x ∈ Ω , t > 0 , w t = Δ ​ w − (

title: Unsupervised Sentence-embeddings by Manifold Approximation and Projection
creator: Subhradeep Kayal
description: Abstract The concept of unsupervised universal sentence encoders has gained traction recently, wherein pre-trained models generate effective task-agnostic fixed-dimensional representations for phrases, sentences and paragraphs. Such methods are of varying complexity, from simple weighted-averages of word vectors to complex language-models based on bidirectional transformers.

title: Quantum Divide and Compute: Exploring The Effect of Different Noise Sources
creator: Thomas Ayral ∗, François-Marie Le Régent, Zain Saleem, Yuri Alexeev, Martin Suchara
description: Abstract Our recent work Ayral2020 showed the first implementation of the Quantum Divide and Compute (QDC) method, which allows to break quantum circuits into smaller fragments with fewer qubits and shallower depth. QDC can thus deal with the limited number of qubits and short coherence times of noisy, intermediate-scale quantum processors.

title: A self-adaptive and robust fission clustering algorithm via heat diffusion and maximal turning angle
creator: Yu Han 1 , Shizhan Lu 2 , Haiyan Xu 1∗
description: Abstract Cluster analysis, which focuses on the grouping and categorization of similar elements, is widely used in various fields of research. A novel and fast clustering algorithm, fission clustering algorithm, is proposed in recent year. In this article, we propose a robust fission clustering (RFC) algorithm and a self-adaptive noise identification method.

title: Simulation electronic thermes of two atoms molecules
creator: Vladimir. P. Koshcheev, Yuriy. N. Shtanov
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Vladimir. P. Koshcheev, Yuriy. N. Shtanov. In the first order of the perturbation theory, the correction to the electronic terms of a diatomic molecule is calculated taking into account the Pauli principle. Keywords: potential interaction energy, Pauli principle, Molière approximation.

title: A characterization of the planes meeting a hyperbolic quadric of PG ​ ( 3 , q ) \mbox{\rm PG}(3,q) in a conic
creator: Bikramaditya Sahu
description: Abstract In this article, a combinatorial characterization of the family of planes of PG ​ ( 3 , q ) \mbox{\rm PG}(3,q) which meet a hyperbolic quadric in an irreducible conic, using their intersection properties with the points and lines of PG ​ ( 3 , q ) \mbox{\rm PG}(3,q) , is given.

title: Exact exponential synchronization rate of high-dimensional Kuramoto models with identical oscillators and digraphs
creator: Shanshan Peng, Jinxing Zhang, Jiandong Zhu, Jianquan Lu, Xiaodi Li
description: Abstract For the high-dimensional Kuramoto model with identical oscillators under a general digraph that has a directed spanning tree, although exponential synchronization was proved under some initial state constraints, the exact exponential synchronization rate has not been revealed until now.

title: Edgeworth approximations for distributions of symmetric statistics Thanks: 1 Research supported by CRC 701
creator: Friedrich Götze 1, Mindaugas Bloznelis 1
description: Abstract . We study the distribution of a general class of asymptotically linear statistics which are symmetric functions of N N independent observations. The distribution functions of these statistics are approximated by an Edgeworth expansion with a remainder of order o ⁡ ( N − 1 ) o(N^{-1}) .

title: The axial charge of the triton from lattice QCD Preprint: ICCUB-21-001 Preprint: FERMILAB-PUB-21-026-T
creator: Assumpta Parreño, Phiala E. Shanahan, Michael L. Wagman, Frank Winter, Emmanuel Chang, William Detmold, Marc Illa, NPLQCD collaboration
description: Abstract The axial charge of the triton is investigated using lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Extending previous work at heavier quark masses, calculations are performed using three ensembles of gauge field configurations generated with quark masses corresponding to a pion mass of 450 MeV.

title: Dimension Free Generalization Bounds for Non Linear Metric Learning
creator: Mark Kozdoba markk@technion.ac.il, Shie Mannor shie@ee.technion.ac.il
description: Abstract In this work we study generalization guarantees for the metric learning problem, where the metric is induced by a neural network type embedding of the data. Specifically, we provide uniform generalization bounds for two regimes – the sparse regime, and a non-sparse regime which we term bounded amplification .

title: Neural Termination Analysis Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3540250.3549120 fse22main-p427-p ISBN: 978-1-4503-9413-0/22/11 Conference: Proceedings of the 30th ACM Joint European Software Engineering Conference and Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering; November 14–18, 2022; Singapore, Singa
creator: Mirco Giacobbe, Daniel Kroening, Julian Parsert
description: Abstract . We introduce a novel approach to the automated termination analysis of computer programs: we use neural networks to represent ranking functions. Ranking functions map program states to values that are bounded from below and decrease as a program runs; the existence of a ranking function proves that the program terminates.

title: Graph Neural Network to Dilute Outliers for Refactoring Monolith Application
creator: Utkarsh Desai, Sambaran Bandyopadhyay, Srikanth Tamilselvam
description: Abstract Microservices are becoming the defacto design choice for software architecture. It involves partitioning the software components into finer modules such that the development can happen independently. It also provides natural benefits when deployed on the cloud since resources can be allocated dynamically to necessary components based on demand.

title: Levitation, oscillations, and wave propagation in a stratified fluid
creator: Marina Carpineti, Fabrizio Croccolo, Alberto Vailati
description: Abstract We present an engaging levitation experiment that students can perform at home or in a simple laboratory using everyday objects. A cork, modified to be slightly denser than water, is placed in a jug containing tap water and coarse kitchen salt delivered at the bottom without stirring.

title: A Thermodynamic Framework for Additive Manufacturing, using Amorphous Polymers, Capable of Predicting Residual Stress, Warpage and Shrinkage
creator: P Sreejith, K Kannan, K R Rajagopal
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by P Sreejith, K Kannan, K R Rajagopal. A thermodynamic framework has been developed for a class of amorphous polymers used in fused deposition modeling (FDM), in order to predict the residual stresses and the accompanying distortion of the geometry of the printed part (warping). When a polymeric melt is cooled, the inhomogeneous distribution of temperature causes spatially varying volumetric shrinkage resulting in the generation of residual stresses.

title: Set-valued Itô’s formula with an application to the general set-valued backward stochastic differential equation Thanks: This work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (11471230, 11671282).
creator: Yao-jia Zhang, Zhun Gou, Nan-jing Huang
description: Abstract Abstract. The overarching goal of this paper is to establish a set-valued Itô’s formula. As an application, we obtain the existence and uniqueness of solutions for the general set-valued backward stochastic differential equation which gives an answer to an open question proposed by Ararat et al. (C. Ararat, J. Ma and W.Q. Wu, Set-valued backward stochastic differential equation, arXiv:2007.15073).

title: First-Order Quantum Correction in Coherent State Expectation Value of Loop-Quantum-Gravity Hamiltonian
creator: Cong Zhang, Shicong Song, Muxin Han
description: Abstract Given the non-graph-changing Hamiltonian H ⁡ [ N ] ^ \widehat{H[N]} in Loop Quantum Gravity (LQG), ⟨ H ⁡ [ N ] ^ ⟩ \langle\widehat{H[N]}\rangle , the coherent state expectation value of H ⁡ [ N ] ^ \widehat{H[N]} , admits an semiclassical expansion in ℓ p 2 \ell^{2}_{\rm p} .

title: Comment on “Faceting and Flattening of Emulsion Droplets: A Mechanical Model”
creator: Pierre A. Haas, Raymond E. Goldstein, Diana Cholakova, Nikolai Denkov, Stoyan K. Smoukov
description: Abstract García-Aguilar et al. García-Aguilar et al. 2021 have shown that the deformations of “shape-shifting droplets”, reported in a series of experimental papers spawned by Refs. Denkov et al. 2015 ; Guttman et al. 2016 , are consistent with an elastic model.

title: Evolution of populations with strategy-dependent time delays
creator: Jacek Miȩkisz, Marek Bodnar
description: Abstract We study effects of strategy-dependent time delays on equilibria of evolving populations. It is well known that time delays may cause oscillations in dynamical systems. Here we report a novel behavior. We show that microscopic models of evolutionary games with strategy-dependent time delays lead to a new type of replicator dynamics.

title: Exact solution of non-Hermitian systems with generalized boundary conditions: size-dependent boundary effect and fragility of skin effect
creator: Cui-Xian Guo, Chun-Hui Liu, Xiao-Ming Zhao, Yanxia Liu, Shu Chen
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Cui-Xian Guo, Chun-Hui Liu, Xiao-Ming Zhao, Yanxia Liu, Shu Chen. Systems with non-Hermitian skin effects are very sensitive to the imposed boundary conditions and lattice size, and thus an important question is whether non-Hermitian skin effects can survive when deviating from the open boundary condition. To unveil the origin of boundary sensitivity, we present exact solutions for one-dimensional non-Hermitian models with generalized boundary conditions and study rigorously the interplay effect of lattice size and boundary terms.

title: Toward an Effective Theory of Neurodynamics: Topological Supersymmetry Breaking, Network Coarse-Graining, and Instanton Interaction
creator: Igor V. Ovchinnikov, Skirmantas Janušonis
description: Abstract Experimental research has shown that the brain’s fast electrochemical dynamics, or neurodynamics (ND), is strongly stochastic, chaotic, and instanton (neuroavalanche)-dominated. It is also partly scale-invariant which has been loosely associated with critical phenomena. It has been recently demonstrated that the supersymmetric theory of stochastics (STS) offers a theoretical framework that can explain all of the above ND features.

title: X-ray Ptychography with a Laboratory Source
creator: Darren J. Batey, Frederic Van Assche, Sander Vanheule, Matthieu N. Boone, Andrew J. Parnell, Oleksandr O. Mykhaylyk, Christoph Rau, Silvia Cipiccia
description: Abstract X-ray ptychography has revolutionised nanoscale phase contrast imaging at large-scale synchrotron sources in recent years. We present here the first successful demonstration of the technique in a small-scale laboratory setting. An experiment was conducted with a liquid metal-jet X-ray source and a single photon-counting detector with a high spectral resolution.

title: A Note on Argumentative Topology: Circularity and Syllogisms as Unsolved Problems
creator: Wlodek W. Zadroznywzadrozn@uncc.edu
description: Abstract In the last couple of years there were a few attempts to apply topological data analysis to text, and in particular to natural language inference. A recent work by Tymochko et al. suggests the possibility of capturing ‘the notion of logical shape in text,’ using ‘topological delay embeddings,’ a technique derived from dynamical systems, applied to word embeddings.

title: Duo property for rings by the quasinilpotent perspective
creator: Abdullah Harmanci, Yosum Kurtulmaz, Burcu Ungor
description: Abstract . In this paper, we focus on the duo ring property via quasinilpotent elements which gives a new kind of generalizations of commutativity. We call this kind of ring qnil-duo . Firstly, some properties of quasinilpotents in a ring are provided.

title: A Joint Inversion-Segmentation approach to Assisted Seismic Interpretation
creator: Matteo Ravasi, Claire Birnie
description: Abstract Structural seismic interpretation and quantitative characterization are historically intertwined processes. The latter provides estimates of properties of the subsurface which can be used to aid structural interpretation alongside the original seismic data and a number of other seismic attributes. In this work, we redefine this process as a inverse problem which tries to jointly estimate subsurface properties (i.e.

title: Spoiler Alert: Using Natural Language Processing to Detect Spoilers in Book Reviews
creator: Marshall HoDepartment of Computer Science
description: Abstract This paper presents an NLP (Natural Language Processing) approach to detecting spoilers in book reviews, using the University of California San Diego (UCSD) Goodreads Spoiler dataset. We explored the use of LSTM, BERT, and RoBERTa language models to perform spoiler detection at the sentence-level.

title: Noise Reduction in X-ray Photon Correlation Spectroscopy with Convolutional Neural Networks Encoder-Decoder Models
creator: Tatiana Konstantinova, Lutz Wiegart, Maksim Rakitin, Anthony M. DeGennaro, Andi M. Barbour
description: Abstract Like other experimental techniques, X-ray Photon Correlation Spectroscopy is subject to various kinds of noise. Random and correlated fluctuations and heterogeneities can be present in a two-time correlation function and obscure the information about the intrinsic dynamics of a sample. Simultaneously addressing the disparate origins of noise in the experimental data is challenging.

title: The phonon mechanism explanation of the superconductivity dichotomy between F ​ e ​ S ​ e FeSe and F ​ e ​ S FeS monolayers on S ​ T ​ O STO and other substrates.
creator: Baruch Rosenstein, B. Ya. Shapiro
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Baruch Rosenstein, B. Ya. Shapiro. It was observed recently (K. Shigekawa et al, PNAS 116, 2470 (2019)) that while monolayer iron chalcigenide F ​ e ​ S ​ e FeSe on S ​ r ​ T ​ i ​ O 3 SrTiO_{3} ( S ​ T ​ O STO ) substrate has a very high critical temperature, its chemical and structural ”twin” material F ​ e ​ S / S ​ T ​ O FeS/STO has a very low T c T_{c} if any.

title: Social dilemmas in off-lattice populations Journal: Chaos Solitons and Fractals
creator: B.F. de Oliveira, A. Szolnoki
description: Abstract Exploring the possible consequences of spatial reciprocity on the evolution of cooperation is an intensively studied research avenue. Related works assumed a certain interaction graph of competing players and studied how particular topologies may influence the dynamical behavior. In this paper we apply a numerically more demanding off-lattice population approach which could be potentially relevant especially in microbiological environments.

title: Model-Augmented Q Q -Learning
creator: Youngmin Oh, Jinwoo Shin, Eunho Yang, Sung Ju Hwang
description: Abstract In recent years, Q Q -learning has become indispensable for model-free reinforcement learning (MFRL). However, it suffers from well-known problems such as under- and overestimation bias of the value, which may adversely affect the policy learning. To resolve this issue, we propose a MFRL framework that is augmented with the components of model-based RL.

title: Entanglement in Cognition violating Bell Inequalities Beyond Cirel’son’s Bound Center Leo Apostel for Interdisciplinary Studies, Free University of Brussels (VUB), Krijgskundestraat 33, 1160 Brussels, Belgium; email addresses: diraerts@vub.ac.be,lestercc21@gmail.com,sgeriente83@yahoo.com School of B
creator: Diederik Aerts, Jonito Aerts Arguëlles, Lester Beltran
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Diederik Aerts, Jonito Aerts Arguëlles, Lester Beltran. We present the results of two tests where a sample of human participants were asked to make judgements about the conceptual combinations The Animal Acts and The Animal eats the Food . Both tests significantly violate the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt version of Bell inequalities (‘CHSH inequality’), thus exhibiting manifestly non-classical behaviour due to the meaning connection between the individual concepts that are combined.

title: Christ–Lee Model: (Anti-)Chiral Supervariable Approach to BRST Formalism
creator: B. Chauhan
description: Abstract Abstract: We derive the off-shell nilpotent of order two and absolutely anti-commuting Becchi-Rouet-Stora-Tyutin (BRST), anti-BRST and (anti-)co-BRST symmetry transformations for the Christ–Lee (CL) model in one (0 + 1)-dimension (1D) of spacetime by exploiting the (anti-)chiral supervariable approach (ACSA) to BRST formalism where the quantum symmetry [i.e. (anti-)BRST along with (anti-)co-BRST] invariant quantities play a crucial role.

title: OPT-GAN: A Broad-Spectrum Global Optimizer for Black-box Problems by Learning Distribution
creator: Minfang Lu, Shuai Ning, Shuangrong Liu, Fengyang Sun, Bo Zhang, Bo Yang, Lin Wang
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Minfang Lu, Shuai Ning, Shuangrong Liu, Fengyang Sun, Bo Zhang, Bo Yang, Lin Wang. Black-box optimization (BBO) algorithms are concerned with finding the best solutions for problems with missing analytical details. Most classical methods for such problems are based on strong and fixed a priori assumptions, such as Gaussianity. However, the complex real-world problems, especially when the global optimum is desired, could be very far from the a priori assumptions because of their diversities, causing unexpected obstacles.

title: In silico model of infection of a CD4(+) T-cell by a human immunodeficiency type 1 virus, and a mini-review on its molecular pathophysiology.
creator: Vivanco-Lira, A. (a.vivancolira@ugto.mx), Nieto-Saucedo, J.R
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Vivanco-Lira, A. (a.vivancolira@ugto.mx), Nieto-Saucedo, J.R. Infection by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus can be defined as a chronic viral infection which mainly affects T-cells; this virus displays a set of both structural and regulatory proteins that aid in its survival within the host’s cell, through these proteins, can the virus alter the host’s gene expression pattern and with it, signaling involved in cell cycle control, cytokine response, differentiation, metabolism, and others; therefore by hijacking the host’s genetic machinery there exists a promotion in viral fitness,

title: Strong Vertices of Doubly Heavy Spin-3/2 Baryons with Light Pseudoscalar Mesons
creator: A. R. Olamaei, K. Azizi, S. Rostami
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by A. R. Olamaei, K. Azizi, S. Rostami. The strong coupling constants are basic quantities that carry information of the strong interactions among the baryon and meson multiplets as well as information on the natures and internal structures of the involved hadrons. These parameters enter to the transition matrix elements of various decays as main inputs and they play key roles in analyses of the experimental data including various hadrons.

title: Anomaly Detection in Energy Usage Patterns
creator: Henry Linder, Nalini Ravishanker, Ming-Hui Chen, David McIntosh, Stanley Nolan
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Henry Linder, Nalini Ravishanker, Ming-Hui Chen, David McIntosh, Stanley Nolan. Energy usage monitoring on higher education campuses is an important step for providing satisfactory service, lowering costs and supporting the move to green energy. We present a collaboration between the Department of Statistics and Facilities Operations at an R1 research university to develop statistically based approaches for monitoring monthly energy usage and proportional yearly usage for several hundred utility accounts on campus.

title: Machine Learning Methods for Histopathological Image Analysis: A Review
creator: Jonathan de Matos *, Steve Tsham Mpinda Ataky, Alceu de Souza Britto Jr, Luiz Eduardo Soares de Oliveira, Alessandro Lameiras Koerich
description: Abstract Histopathological images (HIs) are the gold standard for evaluating some types of tumors for cancer diagnosis. The analysis of such images is not only time and resource consuming, but also very challenging even for experienced pathologists, resulting in inter- and intra-observer disagreements. One of the ways of accelerating such an analysis is to use computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems.

title: Mitigating belief projection in explainable artificial intelligence via Bayesian Teaching
creator: Scott Cheng-Hsin Yang, Wai Keen Vong, Ravi B. Sojitra, Tomas Folke, Patrick Shafto
description: Abstract State-of-the-art deep-learning systems use decision rules that are challenging for humans to model. Explainable AI (XAI) attempts to improve human understanding but rarely accounts for how people typically reason about unfamiliar agents. We propose explicitly modelling the human explainee via Bayesian Teaching, which evaluates explanations by how much they shift explainees’ inferences toward a desired goal.

title: Causal versions of Maximum Entropy and Principle of Insufficient Reason
creator: Dominik Janzing
description: Abstract The Principle of Insufficient Reason (PIR) assigns equal probabilities to each alternative of a random experiment whenever there is no reason to prefer one over the other. The Maximum Entropy Principle (MaxEnt) generalizes PIR to the case where statistical information like expectations are given.

title: Consequences of Misaligned AI
creator: Simon Zhuang, Dylan Hadfield-Menell
description: Abstract AI systems often rely on two key components: a specified goal or reward function and an optimization algorithm to compute the optimal behavior for that goal. This approach is intended to provide value for a principal: the user on whose behalf the agent acts.

title: Grothendieck spaces: the landscape and perspectives Thanks: Research of M. González was partially supported by MICINN (Spain), Grant PID2019-103961GB-C22. T. Kania acknowledges with thanks funding received from SONATA 15 No. 2019/35/D/ST1/01734.
creator: Manuel González, Tomasz Kania
description: Abstract . In 1973, Diestel published his seminal paper Grothendieck spaces and vector measures that drew a connection between Grothendieck spaces (Banach spaces for which weak- and weak*-sequential convergences in the dual space coincide) and vector measures. This connection was developed further in his book with J. Uhl Jr. Vector measures .

title: OBSERVATIONAL SIGNATURES OF TIGHTLY WOUND SPIRALS DRIVEN BY BUOYANCY RESONANCES IN PROTOPLANETARY DISKS FARGO3D ( Benítez-Llambay & Masset 2016 ) , RADMC-3D ( Dullemond et al. 2012 ) , eddy ( Teague 2019 )
creator: Jaehan Bae, Richard Teague, Zhaohuan Zhu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jaehan Bae, Richard Teague, Zhaohuan Zhu. Besides the spirals induced by the Lindblad resonances, planets can generate a family of tightly wound spirals through buoyancy resonances. The excitation of buoyancy resonances depends on the thermal relaxation timescale of the gas.

title: Nonlinear conditions for ultradifferentiability Thanks: AR was supported by FWF-Project P 32905-N, DNN and GS by FWF-Project P 33417-N
creator: David Nicolas Nenning, Armin Rainer, and Gerhard Schindl
description: Abstract . A remarkable theorem of Joris states that a function f f is C ∞ C^{\infty} if two relatively prime powers of f f are C ∞ C^{\infty} . Recently, Thilliez showed that an analogous theorem holds in Denjoy–Carleman classes of Roumieu type.

title: Structured Sparsity Inducing Adaptive Optimizers for Deep Learning
creator: Tristan Deleu, Yoshua Bengio
description: Abstract The parameters of a neural network are naturally organized in groups, some of which might not contribute to its overall performance. To prune out unimportant groups of parameters, we can include some non-differentiable penalty to the objective function, and minimize it using proximal gradient methods.

title: A Short Note on Inadmissible Coefficients of Weight 2 2 and 2 ​ k + 1 2k+1 Newforms

title: Variational Autoencoders:A Hands-Off Approach to Volatility
creator: Maxime Bergeron, Nicholas Fung, John Hull, Zissis Poulos
description: Abstract Maxime Bergeron is the Director of Research and Development at Riskfuel Analytics in Toronto, ON, Canada. mb@riskfuel.com Nicholas Fung is a Masters student in the Edward S. Rogers Sr. Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering at the University of Toronto, and a Research Associate at Riskfuel Analytics in Toronto, ON, Canada. nfung@ece.utoronto.

title: A Convex Optimization Approach to Learning Koopman Operators
creator: M. Sznaier
description: Abstract Koopman operators provide tractable means of learning linear approximations of non-linear dynamics. Many approaches have been proposed to find these operators, typically based upon approximations using an a-priori fixed class of models. However, choosing appropriate models and bounding the approximation error is far from trivial.

title: The low-temperature expansion of the Casimir-Polder free energy of an atom with graphene
creator: Nail Khusnutdinov, Natalia Emelianova
description: Abstract We consider the low-temperature expansion of the Casimir-Polder free energy for an atom and graphene by using the Poisson representation of the free energy. We extend our previous analysis on the different relations between chemical potential μ \mu and mass gap parameter m m .

title: The Spanning Tree Model for the Assembly Kinetics of RNA Viruses.
creator: Inbal Mizrahi, Robijn Bruinsma, Joseph Rudnick
description: Abstract We present a simple kinetic model for the assembly of small single-stranded RNA viruses that can be used to carry out analytical packaging contests between different types of RNA molecules. The RNA selection mechanism is purely kinetic and based on small differences between the assembly energy profiles.

title: Competition Dynamics in the Meme Ecosystem
creator: Trenton Ford, Rachel Krohn, and Tim Weninger Department of Computer Science and Engineering University of Notre Dame {tford5, rkrohn, tweninger}@nd.edu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Trenton Ford, Rachel Krohn, and Tim Weninger Department of Computer Science and Engineering University of Notre Dame {tford5, rkrohn, tweninger}@nd.edu. The creation and sharing of memes is a common modality of online social interactions. The goal of the present work is to better understand the collective dynamics of memes in this accelerating and competitive environment.

title: Increasing the price of a university degree does not significantly affect enrolment if income contingent loans are available: evidence from HECS in Australia
creator: Fabio I. Martinenghi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Fabio I. Martinenghi. I provide evidence that, when income-contingent loans are available, student enrolment in university courses is not significantly affected by large increases in the price of those courses. I use publicly available domestic enrolment data from Australia. I study whether large increases in the price of higher education for selected disciplines in Australia in 2009 and in 2012 was associated with changes in their enrolment growth.
