The author thank
creator: Alessio Muscillo
description: Abstract In this note I derive simple formulas based on the adjacency matrix of a network to compute measures associated with Ronald S. Burt’s structural holes (effective size, redundancy, local constraint and constraint). This can help to interpret these measures and also to define naive algorithms for their computation based on matrix operations.

title: Collective neutrino oscillations accounting for neutrino quantum decoherence
creator: Alexander Studenikin
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alexander Studenikin. In our previous studies (see [ 1 ] and references therein) we developed a new theoretical framework that enabled one to consider a new mechanism of neutrino quantum decoherence engendered by the neutrino radiative decay. In parallel, another framework was developed (see [ 2 ] and references therein) for the description of the neutrino quantum decoherence due to the non-forward neutrino scattering processes. Both mechanisms are described by the master equations in the Lindblad form.

title: Using Deep LSD to build operators in GANs latent space with meaning in real space
creator: J. Quetzalcóatl Toledo-Marín, James A. Glazier
description: Abstract Generative models rely on the key idea that data can be represented in terms of latent variables which are uncorrelated by definition. Lack of correlation is important because it suggests that the latent space manifold is simpler to understand and manipulate. Generative models are widely used in deep learning, e.g. , variational autoencoders (VAEs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs).

title: Adversarial Perturbations Are Not So Weird: Entanglement of Robust and Non-Robust Features in Neural Network Classifiers
creator: Jacob M. Springer, Melanie Mitchell, Garrett T. Kenyon
description: Abstract Neural networks trained on visual data are well-known to be vulnerable to often imperceptible adversarial perturbations. The reasons for this vulnerability are still being debated in the literature. Recently Ilyas et al. 2019 showed that this vulnerability arises, in part, because neural network classifiers rely on highly predictive but brittle “non-robust” features.

title: Energetic cost of Hamiltonian quantum gates
creator: Sebastian Deffner
description: Abstract Landauer’s principle laid the main foundation for the development of modern thermodynamics of information. However, in its original inception the principle relies on semiformal arguments and dissipative dynamics. Hence, if and how Landauer’s principle applies to unitary quantum computing is less than obvious.

title: Backdoor Scanning for Deep Neural Networks through K-Arm Optimization
creator: Guangyu Shen, Yingqi Liu, Guanhong Tao, Shengwei An, Qiuling Xu, Siyuan Cheng, Shiqing Ma, Xiangyu Zhang
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Guangyu Shen, Yingqi Liu, Guanhong Tao, Shengwei An, Qiuling Xu, Siyuan Cheng, Shiqing Ma, Xiangyu Zhang. Back-door attack poses a severe threat to deep learning systems. It injects hidden malicious behaviors to a model such that any input stamped with a special pattern can trigger such behaviors. Detecting back-door is hence of pressing need.

title: High-Frequency Instabilities of a Boussinesq-Whitham System: A Perturbative Approach
creator: Ryan Creedon 1 , Bernard Deconinck 2 , Olga Trichtchenko 3 1 Dept. of Applied Mathematics, U. of Washington, Seattle, WA, 98105, USA ( creedon@uw.edu ) 2 Dept. of Applied Mathematics, U. of Washington, Seattle, WA, 98105, USA ( deconinc@uw.edu ) 3 Dept. of Physics and Astronomy, U. of Western Ontari
description: Abstract . We analyze the spectral stability of small-amplitude, periodic, traveling-wave solutions of a Boussinesq-Whitham system. These solutions are shown numerically to exhibit high-frequency instabilities when subject to bounded perturbations on the real line. We use a formal perturbation method to estimate the asymptotic behavior of these instabilities in the small-amplitude regime.

title: DARE-SLAM: Degeneracy-Aware and Resilient Loop Closing in Perceptually-Degraded Environments Thanks: The research was carried out at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology, under a contract with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. This work was partially fun
creator: Kamak Ebadi, Matteo Palieri, Sally Wood, Curtis Padgett, Ali-akbar Agha-mohammadi
description: Abstract Enabling fully autonomous robots capable of navigating and exploring large-scale, unknown and complex environments has been at the core of robotics research for several decades. A key requirement in autonomous exploration is building accurate and consistent maps of the unknown environment that can be used for reliable navigation.

title: Negative Data Augmentation
creator: Abhishek Sinha, Kumar Ayush, Jiaming Song, Burak Uzkent, Hongxia Jin, Stefano Ermon, Department of Computer ScienceStanford University{a7b23, kayush, tsong, buzkent, ermon}@stanford.edu, Samsung Research America
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Abhishek Sinha, Kumar Ayush, Jiaming Song, Burak Uzkent, Hongxia Jin, Stefano Ermon, Department of Computer ScienceStanford University{a7b23, kayush, tsong, buzkent, ermon}@stanford.edu, Samsung Research America. Data augmentation is often used to enlarge datasets with synthetic samples generated in accordance with the underlying data distribution. To enable a wider range of augmentations, we explore negative data augmentation strategies (NDA) that intentionally create out-of-distribution samples.

title: The Cognition of Counterexample in Mathematics Students
creator: Shannon Ezzat, Scott Rodney
description: Abstract . Studying Mathematics requires a synthesis of skills from a multitude of academic disciplines; logical reasoning being chief among them. This paper explores mathematical logical preparedness of students entering first year university mathematics courses and also the effectiveness of using logical facility to predict successful course outcomes.

title: Decontextualization: Making Sentences Stand-Alone
creator: Eunsol Choi, Jennimaria Palomaki, Matthew Lamm, Tom Kwiatkowski, Dipanjan Das, Michael Collins
description: Abstract Models for question answering, dialogue agents, and summarization often interpret the meaning of a sentence in a rich context and use that meaning in a new context. Taking excerpts of text can be problematic, as key pieces may not be explicit in a local window.

title: Toward Safe and Efficient Human–Robot Interaction via Behavior-Driven Danger Signaling
creator: Mehdi Hosseinzadeh, Bruno Sinopoli, Aaron F. Bobick
description: Abstract This paper introduces the notion of danger awareness in the context of Human-Robot Interaction (HRI), which decodes whether a human is aware of the existence of the robot, and illuminates whether the human is willing to engage in enforcing the safety.

title: Charged dust solutions for the warp drive spacetime
creator: Osvaldo L. Santos-Pereira, Everton M. C. Abreu, Marcelo B. Ribeiro
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Osvaldo L. Santos-Pereira, Everton M. C. Abreu, Marcelo B. Ribeiro. The Alcubierre warp drive metric is a spacetime construction where a massive particle located inside a spacetime distortion, called warp bubble, travels at velocities arbitrarily higher than the velocity of light. This theoretically constructed spacetime geometry is a consequence of general relativity where global superluminal velocities, also known as warp speeds, are possible, whereas local speeds are limited to subluminal ones as required by special relativity.

title: Inverse design of plasma metamaterial devices for optical computing
creator: Jesse A. Rodríguez, Ahmed I. Abdalla, Benjamin Wang, Beicheng Lou, Shanhui Fan, Mark A. Cappelli
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jesse A. Rodríguez, Ahmed I. Abdalla, Benjamin Wang, Beicheng Lou, Shanhui Fan, Mark A. Cappelli. We apply inverse design methods to produce two-dimensional plasma metamaterial (PMM) devices. Backpropagated finite difference frequency domain (FDFD) simulations are used to design waveguides and demultiplexers operating under both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) modes. Demultiplexing and waveguiding are demonstrated for devices composed of plasma elements with reasonable plasma densities ∼ 7 \sim 7 GHz, allowing for future in-situ training and experimental realization of these designs.

title: Energetic Electron Distribution of the Coronal Acceleration Region: First results from Joint Microwave and Hard X-ray Imaging Spectroscopy Journal: ApJL Facilities: OVRO:SA, RHESSI, SDO, Hinode Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , CASA ( McMullin et al. 2007 ) , LMFIT ( Newville et al. 20
creator: Bin Chen (陈彬), Marina Battaglia, Säm Krucker, Katharine K. Reeves, Lindsay Glesener
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Bin Chen (陈彬), Marina Battaglia, Säm Krucker, Katharine K. Reeves, Lindsay Glesener. Nonthermal sources located above bright flare arcades, referred to as the “above-the-loop-top” sources, have been often suggested as the primary electron acceleration site in major solar flares. The X8.2 limb flare on 2017 September 10 features such an above-the-loop-top source, which was observed in both microwaves and hard X-rays (HXRs) by the Expanded Owens Valley Solar Array (EOVSA) and the Reuven Ramaty High Energy Solar Spectroscopic Imager (RHESSI), respectively.

title: Transfer learning based few-shot classification using optimal transport mapping from preprocessed latent space of backbone neural network
creator: Tomáš Chobola, Daniel Vašata, Pavel Kordík
description: Abstract MetaDL Challenge 2020 focused on image classification tasks in few-shot settings. This paper describes second best submission in the competition. Our meta learning approach modifies the distribution of classes in a latent space produced by a backbone network for each class in order to better follow the Gaussian distribution.

title: Locally Adaptive Label Smoothing for Predictive Churn
creator: Dara Bahri, Heinrich Jiang
description: Abstract Training modern neural networks is an inherently noisy process that can lead to high prediction churn – disagreements between re-trainings of the same model due to factors such as randomization in the parameter initialization and mini-batches– even when the trained models all attain similar accuracies. Such prediction churn can be very undesirable in practice.

title: A note on the low-dimensional Minkowski-reduction
creator: Á. G.Horváth
description: Abstract . In this paper, we recall the basic results of the reduction theory of positive definite quadratic forms. Since finding the shortest vectors in a lattice is an NP-hard problem, the low-dimensional results in lattice reduction theory have an important role.

title: Global solutions of the two-dimensional Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation with a linearly growing mode in each direction Thanks: ∗ corresponding author
creator: David M. Ambrose ∗, Anna L. Mazzucato
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by David M. Ambrose ∗, Anna L. Mazzucato. We consider the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation in two space dimension. We establish the first proof of global existence of solutions in the presence of a linearly growing mode in both spatial directions for sufficiently small data. We develop a new method to this end, categorizing wavenumbers as low (linearly growing modes), intermediate (linearly decaying modes that serve as energy sinks for the low modes), and high (strongly linearly decaying modes).

title: Quantum mechanical study of the attosecond nonlinear Fourier transform spectroscopy of carbon dioxide
creator: Sergy Yu. Grebenshchikov, Sergio Carbajo
description: Abstract Attosecond nonlinear Fourier transform (NFT) pump probe spectroscopy is an experimental technique which allows investigation of the electronic excitation, ionization, and unimolecular dissociation processes. The NFT spectroscopy utilizes ultrafast multiphoton ionization in the extreme ultraviolet spectral range and detects the dissociation products of the unstable ionized species.

title: Pulse interactions in weakly nonlinear coherent optical communication links
creator: J Gibney 1, I A Kuk 2 and I R Gabitov 1,2
description: Abstract The intrachannel interaction of pulses in weakly nonlinear coherent optical fiber lines is theoretically investigated. It is shown that the main contribution to the perturbation of the optical field comes from resonant interactions of ordered triplets of pulses. The structure of triplets is determined. The weight contributions of such interactions are calculated.

title: Discrete Bessel and Mathieu functions
description: Abstract The two-dimensional Helmholtz equation separates in elliptic coordinates based on two distinct foci, a limit case of which includes polar coordinate systems when the two foci coalesce. This equation is invariant under the Euclidean group of translations and orthogonal transformations; we replace the latter by the discrete dihedral group of N N discrete rotations and reflections.

title: 𝒫 \mathcal{P} , 𝒯 \mathcal{T} -odd Faraday rotation in intracavity absorption spectroscopy with molecular beam as a possible way to improve the sensitivity of the search for the time reflection noninvariant effects in nature
creator: D. V. Chubukov 1,2 , L. V. Skripnikov 1,2 , A. N. Petrov 1,2 , V. N. Kutuzov 1 , L. N. Labzowsky 1,2
description: Abstract The present constraint on the space parity ( 𝒫 \mathcal{P} ) and time reflection invariance ( 𝒯 \mathcal{T} ) violating electron electric dipole moment ( e e EDM) is based on the observation of the electron spin precession in an external electric field using the ThO molecule.

title: CoIL: Coordinate-based Internal Learning for Imaging Inverse Problems
creator: Yu Sun, Jiaming Liu, Mingyang Xie, Brendt Wohlberg, and Ulugbek S. Kamilov
description: Abstract We propose Coordinate-based Internal Learning (CoIL) as a new deep-learning (DL) methodology for continuous representation of measurements. Unlike traditional DL methods that learn a mapping from the measurements to the desired image, CoIL trains a multilayer perceptron (MLP) to encode the complete measurement field by mapping the coordinates of the measurements to their responses.

title: Extensions of Watson’s theorem and the Ramanujan-Guinand formula Thanks: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification. Primary 11M06, 33E20; Secondary 33C10. Keywords and phrases. Watson’s lemma, Ramanujan-Guinand formula, Poisson summation formula, Generalized modified Bessel function
creator: Rahul Kumar
description: Abstract . Ramanujan provided several results involving the modified Bessel function K z ​ ( x ) K_{z}(x) in his Lost Notebook. One of them is the famous Ramanujan-Guinand formula, equivalent to the functional equation of the non-holomorphic Eiesenstien series on S ​ L 2 ​ ( z ) SL_{2}(z) .

title: Star-topology Registers: NMR and Quantum Information Perspectives
creator: T S Mahesh, Deepak Khurana, Krithika V R, Sreejith G J, C S Sudheer Kumar
description: Abstract Quantum control of large spin registers is crucial for many applications ranging from spectroscopy to quantum information. A key factor that determines the efficiency of a register for implementing a given information processing task is its network topology. One particular type, called star-topology, involves a central qubit uniformly interacting with a set of ancillary qubits.

title: Benchmarks, Algorithms, and Metrics for Hierarchical Disentanglement
creator: Andrew Slavin Ross, Finale Doshi-Velez
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Andrew Slavin Ross, Finale Doshi-Velez. In representation learning, there has been recent interest in developing algorithms to disentangle the ground-truth generative factors behind a dataset, and metrics to quantify how fully this occurs. However, these algorithms and metrics often assume that both representations and ground-truth factors are flat, continuous, and factorized, whereas many real-world generative processes involve rich hierarchical structure, mixtures of discrete and continuous variables with dependence between them, and even varying intrinsic dimensionality.

title: Culture-inspired Multi-modal Color Palette Generation and Colorization: A Chinese Youth Subculture Case
creator: Yufan Li, Jinggang Zhuo, Ling Fan, Harry Jiannan Wang
description: Abstract Color is an essential component of graphic design, acting not only as a visual factor but also carrying cultural implications. However, existing research on algorithmic color palette generation and colorization largely ignores the cultural aspect. In this paper, we contribute to this line of research by first constructing a unique color dataset inspired by a specific culture, i.e.

title: D2A U-Net: Automatic Segmentation of COVID-19 Lesions from CT Slices with Dilated Convolution and Dual Attention Mechanism
creator: Xiangyu Zhao, Peng Zhang, Fan Song, Guangda Fan, Yangyang Sun, Yujia Wang, Zheyuan Tian, Luqi Zhang, Guanglei Zhang
description: Abstract Background and Objective : Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) has caused great casualties and becomes almost the most urgent public health events worldwide. Computed tomography (CT) is a significant screening tool for COVID-19 infection, and automated segmentation of lung infection in COVID-19 CT images will greatly assist diagnosis and health care of patients.

title: On the Hardness of PAC-learning Stabilizer States with Noise
creator: Aravind Gollakota, Daniel Liang
description: Abstract We consider the problem of learning stabilizer states with noise in the Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) framework of Aaronson 2007 for learning quantum states. In the noiseless setting, an algorithm for this problem was recently given by Rocchetto 2018 , but the noisy case was left open.

title: Non-flow effects in correlation between harmonic flow and transverse momentum in nuclear collisions
creator: Chunjian Zhang, Arabinda Behera, Somadutta Bhatta, Jiangyong Jia
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chunjian Zhang, Arabinda Behera, Somadutta Bhatta, Jiangyong Jia. A large anti-correlation signal between elliptic flow v 2 v_{2} and average transverse momentum [ p T ] [p_{\mathrm{T}}] was recently measured in small collision systems, consistent with a final-state hydrodynamic response to the initial geometry. This negative v 2 v_{2} – [ p T ] [p_{\mathrm{T}}] correlation was predicted to change to positive correlation for events with very small charged particle multiplicity N ch N_{\mathrm{ch}} due to initial-state momentum anisotropies of the gluon saturation effects.

title: Neural Network flows of low q q -state Potts and clock Models
creator: Dimitrios Giataganas, Ching-Yu Huang, Feng-Li Lin
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Dimitrios Giataganas, Ching-Yu Huang, Feng-Li Lin. It is known that a trained Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM) on the binary Monte Carlo Ising spin configurations, generates a series of iterative reconstructed spin configurations which spontaneously flow and stabilize to the critical point of physical system. Here we construct a variety of Neural Network (NN) flows using the RBM and (variational) autoencoders, to study the q q -state Potts and clock models on the square lattice for q = 2 , 3 , 4 q=2,3,4 .

title: Observability for the Schrödinger Equation: an Optimal Transportation Approach
creator: François Golse, Thierry Paul
description: Abstract . We establish an observation inequality for the Schrödinger equation on 𝐑 d \mathbf{R}^{d} , uniform in the Planck constant ℏ ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] \hbar\in[0,1] . The proof is based on the pseudometric introduced in [F. Golse, T. Paul, Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 223 (2017), 57–94].

title: Extracting Rationale for Open Source Software Development Decisions — A Study of Python Email Archives
creator: Pankajeshwara Nand Sharma 1 , Bastin Tony Roy Savarimuthu 2 , Nigel Stanger 3
description: Abstract A sound Decision-Making (DM) process is key to the successful governance of software projects. In many Open Source Software Development (OSSD) communities, DM processes lie buried amongst vast amounts of publicly available data. Hidden within this data lie the rationale for decisions that led to the evolution and maintenance of software products.

title: An Interactive Proof of Termination for a Concurrent λ \lambda -calculus with References and Explicit Substitutions
creator: Yann Hamdaoui, Benoît Valiron
description: Abstract In this paper we introduce a typed, concurrent λ \lambda -calculus with references featuring explicit substitutions for variables and references. Alongside usual safety properties, we recover strong normalization. The proof is based on a reducibility technique and an original interactive property reminiscent of the Game Semantics approach.

title: GitHub Discussions: An Exploratory Study of Early Adoption
creator: Hideaki Hata, Nicole Novielli, Sebastian Baltes, Raula Gaikovina Kula, Christoph Treude
description: Abstract Discussions is a new feature of GitHub for asking questions or discussing topics outside of specific Issues or Pull Requests. Before being available to all projects in December 2020, it had been tested on selected open source software projects.

title: Fisher Scoring for crossed factor Linear Mixed Models
creator: Thomas Maullin-Sapey, Thomas E. Nichols
description: Abstract The analysis of longitudinal, heterogeneous or unbalanced clustered data is of primary importance to a wide range of applications. The Linear Mixed Model (LMM) is a popular and flexible extension of the linear model specifically designed for such purposes.

title: Quincke oscillations of colloids at planar electrodes
creator: Zhengyan Zhang, Hang Yuan, Yong Dou, Monica Olvera de la Cruz, Kyle J. M. Bishop
description: Abstract Dielectric particles in weakly conducting fluids rotate spontaneously when subject to strong electric fields. Such Quincke rotation near a plane electrode leads to particle translation that enables physical models of active matter. Here, we show that Quincke rollers can also exhibit oscillatory dynamics, whereby particles move back and forth about a fixed location.

title: Attentive Gaussian processes for probabilistic time-series generation
creator: Kuilin Chen, Chi-Guhn Lee
description: Abstract The transduction of sequence has been mostly done by recurrent networks, which are computationally demanding and often underestimate uncertainty severely. We propose a computationally efficient attention-based network combined with the Gaussian process regression to generate real-valued sequence, which we call the Attentive-GP.

title: Early Abandoning and Pruning for Elastic Distances including Dynamic Time Warping Thanks: This research has been supported by Australian Research Council grant DP210100072.
creator: Matthieu Herrmann, Geoffrey I. Webb
description: Abstract Nearest neighbor search under elastic distances is a key tool for time series analysis, supporting many applications. However, straightforward implementations of distances require O ⁡ ( n 2 ) O(n^{2}) space and time complexities, preventing these applications from scaling to long series.

title: Time dependent Quantum Perturbations uniform in the semiclassical regime
creator: François Golse, Thierry Paul
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by François Golse, Thierry Paul. We present a time dependent quantum perturbation result, uniform in the Planck constant, for perturbations of potentials whose gradients are Lipschitz continuous by potentials whose gradients are only bounded a.e..

title: SensPick: Sens e Pick ing for Word Sense Disambiguation
creator: Sm Zobaed 1 , Md Enamul Haque 2 , Md Fazle Rabby 1 , and Mohsen Amini Salehi 1
description: Abstract Word sense disambiguation (WSD) methods identify the most suitable meaning of a word with respect to the usage of that word in a specific context. Neural network-based WSD approaches rely on a sense-annotated corpus since they do not utilize lexical resources.

title: Slow wave and truly rainbow trapping in one-way terahertz waveguide
creator: Jie Xu,
description: Abstract Abstract Slow or even stop electromagnetic (EM) waves attract researchers’ attentions for its potential applications in energy storage, optical buffer and nonlinearity enhancement. However, in most cases of the EM waves trapping, the EM waves are not truly trapped due to the existence of reflection.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Optimized Beam Training in Multi-Hop Terahertz Communications This research was supported by the U.S. National Science Foundation under Grants CNS-1941348 and CNS-2008646.
creator: Arian Ahmadi and Omid Semiari
description: Abstract Communication at terahertz (THz) frequency bands is a promising solution for achieving extremely high data rates in next-generation wireless networks. While the THz communication is conventionally envisioned for short-range wireless applications due to the high atmospheric absorption at THz frequencies, multi-hop directional transmissions can be enabled to extend the communication range.

title: The second vanishing theorem in Stanley-Reisner ring with topological interpretation
creator: Rajsekhar Bhattacharyya
description: Abstract . For regular local ring, the “second vanishing theorem” or “SVT” of local cohomology has been proved in several cases. In this paper, we explore the result similar to that of the SVT to Stanley-Reisner ring with an interpretation from combinatorial topology. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 13D45 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 13D45 1.

title: Constraints on the Symmetry Energy from PREX-II in the Multimessenger Era
creator: Tong-Gang Yue 1, Lie-Wen Chen 1, Zhen Zhang 2, Ying Zhou 3
description: Abstract The neutron skin thickness Δ ​ r np \Delta r_{\rm{np}} of heavy nuclei is essentially determined by the symmetry energy density slope L ⁡ ( ρ ) L({\rho}) at ρ c = 0.11 ​ fm − 3 ≈ 2 / 3 ​ ρ 0 \rho_{c}=0.

title: Proximal Decoding for LDPC-coded Massive MIMO Channels
creator: Tadashi Wadayama and Satoshi Takabe
description: Abstract We propose a novel optimization-based decoding algorithm for LDPC-coded massive MIMO channels. The proposed decoding algorithm is based on a proximal gradient method for solving an approximate maximum a posteriori (MAP) decoding problem. The key idea is the use of a code-constraint polynomial penalizing a vector far from a codeword as a regularizer in the approximate MAP objective function.

title: Doublon-like excitations and their phononic coupling in a Mott charge-density-wave system
creator: C. J. Butler, M. Yoshida, T. Hanaguri, Y. Iwasa
description: Abstract Electron-phonon-driven charge density waves can in some circumstances allow electronic correlations to become predominant, driving a system into a Mott insulating state. New insights into both the Mott state and preceding charge density wave may result from observations of the coupled dynamics of their underlying degrees of freedom.

title: Fast Deterministic Approximation of Symmetric Indefinite Kernel Matrices with High Dimensional Datasets
creator: Difeng Cai, James Nagy †, Yuanzhe Xi †
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Difeng Cai, James Nagy †, Yuanzhe Xi †. Kernel methods are used frequently in various applications of machine learning. For large-scale high dimensional applications, the success of kernel methods hinges on the ability to operate certain large dense kernel matrix K K . An enormous amount of literature has been devoted to the study of symmetric positive semi-definite (SPSD) kernels, where Nyström methods compute a low-rank approximation to the kernel matrix via choosing landmark points.

title: If you cite this paper, please use the following reference: Ryo Kawaoka, Daiki Chiba, Takuya Watanabe, Mitsuaki Akiyama, and Tatsuya Mori “A First Look at COVID-19 Domain Names: Origin and Implications,” In Proceedings of the Passive and Active Measurement Conference 2021 (PAM 2021) A First Look at
creator: Ryo Kawaoka, Daiki Chiba, Takuya Watanabe, Mitsuaki Akiyama, Tatsuya Mori
description: Abstract This work takes a first look at domain names related to COVID-19 (Cov19doms in short), using a large-scale registered Internet domain name database, which accounts for 260M of distinct domain names registered for 1.6K of distinct top-level domains. We extracted 167K of Cov19doms that have been registered between the end of December 2019 and the end of September 2020.

title: Bayesian Knockoff Filter
creator: Jiaqi Gu, Guosheng Yin
description: Abstract In many scientific fields, researchers are interested in discovering features with substantial effect on the response from a large number of features while controlling the proportion of false discoveries. By incorporating the knockoff procedure in the Bayesian framework, we develop the Bayesian knockoff filter (BKF) for selecting features that have important effect on the response.

title: Optimal Design of Membrane Cascades for Gaseous and Liquid Mixtures via MINLP
creator: Jose Adrian Chavez Velasco ‡, Radhakrishna Tumbalam Gooty ‡, Mohit Tawarmalani †, Rakesh Agrawal ∗
description: Abstract Given the growing concern of reducing CO 2 emissions, it is desirable to identify, for a given separation carried out through a membrane cascade, the optimum design that yields the lowest energy consumption. Nevertheless, designing a membrane cascade is challenging since, there are often multiple feasible configurations that differ in their energy consumption and cost.

title: Robust Federated Learning with Attack-Adaptive Aggregation
creator: Ching Pui Wan, Qifeng Chen
description: Abstract Federated learning is vulnerable to various attacks, such as model poisoning and backdoor attacks, even if some existing defense strategies are used. To address this challenge, we propose an attack-adaptive aggregation strategy to defend against various attacks for robust federated learning.

title: Reconstruction of Primordial Power Spectrum of curvature perturbation from the merger rate of Primordial Black Hole Binaries
creator: Rampei Kimura 1 , Teruaki Suyama 2 , Masahide Yamaguchi 2 and Ying-li Zhang 3,4
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Rampei Kimura 1 , Teruaki Suyama 2 , Masahide Yamaguchi 2 and Ying-li Zhang 3,4. The properties of primordial curvature perturbations on small scales are still unknown while those on large scales have been well probed by the observations of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies and the large scale structure.

title: Narrowing the mass range of Fuzzy Dark Matter with Ultra-faint Dwarfs
creator: Kohei Hayashi, Elisa G. M. Ferreira, Hei Yin Jowett Chan
description: Abstract Fuzzy dark matter (FDM) is an attractive dark matter candidate motivated by small scale problems in astrophysics and with a rich phenomenology on those scales. We scrutinize the FDM model, more specifically the mass of the FDM particle, through a dynamical analysis for the Galactic ultra-faint dwarf (UFD) galaxies.

title: Small scale formations in the incompressible porous media equation Thanks: Department of Mathematics, Duke University, 120 Science Dr., Durham NC 27708, USA; email: kiselev@math.duke.edu Thanks: School of Mathematics, Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA 30332, USA; email: yaoyao@math.gatech
creator: Alexander Kiselev, Yao Yao
description: Abstract . We construct examples of solutions to the incompressible porous media (IPM) equation that must exhibit infinite in time growth of derivatives provided they remain smooth. As an application, this allows us to obtain nonlinear instability for a class of stratified steady states of IPM. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 35Q35,76B03 1.

title: Biomedical Question Answering: A Survey of Approaches and Challenges Biomedical Question Answering: A Survey of Approaches and Challenges CCS: Applied computing Life and medical sciences CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning CCS: Computing methodologies Natural language processing
creator: Qiao Jin, Zheng Yuan, Guangzhi Xiong, Qianlan Yu, Huaiyuan Ying, Chuanqi Tan, Mosha Chen, Songfang Huang, Xiaozhong Liu, Sheng Yu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Qiao Jin, Zheng Yuan, Guangzhi Xiong, Qianlan Yu, Huaiyuan Ying, Chuanqi Tan, Mosha Chen, Songfang Huang, Xiaozhong Liu, Sheng Yu. Automatic Question Answering (QA) has been successfully applied in various domains such as search engines and chatbots. Biomedical QA (BQA), as an emerging QA task, enables innovative applications to effectively perceive, access and understand complex biomedical knowledge.

title: Cloud Parameterizations and their Effect on Retrievals of Exoplanet Reflection Spectroscopy
creator: Sagnick Mukherjee 1,2 , Natasha E. Batalha 3 , Mark S. Marley 3
description: Abstract Future space-based direct imaging missions will perform low-resolution (R < < 100) optical (0.3-1 μ \mu m) spectroscopy of planets, thus enabling reflected spectroscopy of cool giants. Reflected light spectroscopy is encoded with rich information about the scattering and absorbing properties of planet atmospheres.

title: Enabling Multi-programming Mechanism for Quantum Computing in the NISQ Era
creator: Siyuan Niu, Aida Todri-Sanial
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Siyuan Niu, Aida Todri-Sanial. NISQ devices have several physical limitations and unavoidable noisy quantum operations, and only small circuits can be executed on a quantum machine to get reliable results. This leads to the quantum hardware under-utilization issue. Here, we address this problem and improve the quantum hardware throughput by proposing a Quantum Multi-programming Compiler (QuMC) to execute multiple quantum circuits on quantum hardware simultaneously. This approach can also reduce the total runtime of circuits.

title: Improving the accuracy of the energy estimation by combining quantum annealing with classical computation
creator: Takashi Imoto, Yuya Seki, Yuichiro Matsuzaki, Shiro Kawabata
description: Abstract Quantum chemistry calculations are important applications of quantum annealing. For practical applications in quantum chemistry, it is essential to estimate a ground state energy of the Hamiltonian with chemical accuracy. However, there are no known methods to guarantee the accuracy of the estimation of the energy calculated by quantum annealing.

title: A Linear Input Dependence Model for Interdependent Networks
creator: Hemanshu Kaul, Adam Rumpf
description: Abstract We consider a linear relaxation of a generalized minimum-cost network flow problem with binary input dependencies. In this model the flows through certain arcs are bounded by linear (or more generally, piecewise linear concave) functions of the flows through other arcs.

title: Thermodynamics of Exotic Black Holes in Lovelock Gravity
creator: Brayden Hull, Robert B. Mann
description: Abstract We examine the thermodynamics of a new class of asymptotically AdS black holes with non-constant curvature event horizons in Gauss-Bonnet Lovelock gravity, with the cosmological constant acting as thermodynamic pressure. We find that non-trivial curvature on the horizon can significantly affect their thermodynamic behaviour.

title: RCC calculation of electric dipole polarizability and correlation energy of Cn, Nh + and Og: Correlation effects from lighter to superheavy elements
creator: Ravi Kumar, S. Chattopadhyay, D. Angom, B. K. Mani
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ravi Kumar, S. Chattopadhyay, D. Angom, B. K. Mani. We employ a fully relativistic coupled-cluster theory to calculate the ground-state electric dipole polarizability and electron correlation energy of superheavy elements Cn, Nh + and Og. To assess the trend of electron correlation as function of Z Z , we also calculate the correlation energies for three lighter homologs–Zn, Cd and Hg; Ga + , In + and Tl + ; Kr, Xe and Rn–for each superheavy elements.

title: Velocity-vorticity-pressure formulation for the Oseen problem with variable viscosity Thanks: Updated: August 9, 2026.
creator: V. Anaya, R. Caraballo, B. Gómez-Vargas, D. Mora, R. Ruiz-Baier
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by V. Anaya, R. Caraballo, B. Gómez-Vargas, D. Mora, R. Ruiz-Baier. We propose and analyse an augmented mixed finite element method for the Oseen equations written in terms of velocity, vorticity, and pressure with non-constant viscosity and homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition for the velocity. The weak formulation includes least-squares terms arising from the constitutive equation and from the incompressibility condition, and we show that it satisfies the hypotheses of the Babuška-Brezzi theory.

title: Orbital order in a bosonic p p -band triangular lattice
creator: Hua Chen, X. C. Xie
description: Abstract We present a detailed study of the Bose-Hubbard model in a p p -band triangular lattice by focusing on the evolution of orbital order across the superfluid-Mott insulator transition. Two distinct phases are found in the superfluid regime. One of these phases adiabatically connects the weak interacting limit.

title: Quality Assurance for AI-based Systems: Overview and Challenges
creator: Michael Felderer, Rudolf Ramler
description: Abstract The number and importance of AI-based systems in all domains is growing. With the pervasive use and the dependence on AI-based systems, the quality of these systems becomes essential for their practical usage. However, quality assurance for AI-based systems is an emerging area that has not been well explored and requires collaboration between the SE and AI research communities.

title: A Comprehensive Power Spectral Density Analysis of Astronomical Time Series. II. The Swift/BAT Long Gamma-Ray Bursts Mathematica ( Wolfram Research 2016 , v10.4; ) , SciPy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 , v1.1.0; ) , wavepal ( Lenoir & Crucifix 2018a ; Lenoir & Crucifix 2018b )
creator: Mariusz Tarnopolski, Volodymyr Marchenko
description: Abstract We investigated the prompt light curves (LCs) of long gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) from the Swift/BAT catalog. We aimed to characterize their power spectral densities (PSDs), search for quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs), and conduct novel analyses directly in the time domain. We analyzed the PSDs using Lomb-Scargle periodograms, and searched for QPOs using wavelet scalograms.

title: Language Models for Lexical Inference in Context
creator: Martin Schmitt, Hinrich SchützeCenter for Information and Language Processing (CIS)LMU Munich, Germany
description: Abstract Lexical inference in context (LIiC) is the task of recognizing textual entailment between two very similar sentences, i.e., sentences that only differ in one expression. It can therefore be seen as a variant of the natural language inference task that is focused on lexical semantics.

title: Risk-Averse Offline Reinforcement Learning
creator: Núria Armengol Urpí, Sebastian Curi, Andreas Krause
description: Abstract Training Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents online in high-stakes applications is often prohibitive due to the risk associated with exploration. Thus, the agent can only use data previously collected by safe policies. While previous work considers optimizing the average performance using offline data, we focus on optimizing a risk-averse criterion.

title: Stability of SGD: Tightness Analysis and Improved Bounds
creator: Yikai Zhang, Wenjia Zhang ∗, Sammy Bald ∗, Vamsi Pingali, Chao Chen, Mayank Goswami
description: Abstract Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) based methods have been widely used for training large-scale machine learning models that also generalize well in practice. Several explanations have been offered for this generalization performance, a prominent one being algorithmic stability [ 18 ] .

title: Large-scale GHZ states through topologically protected zero-energy mode in a superconducting qutrit-resonator chain
creator: Jin-Xuan Han 1, Jin-Lei Wu 1, Yan Wang 1, Yan Xia 2, Yong-Yuan Jiang 1, Jie Song 1,3,4,5
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jin-Xuan Han 1, Jin-Lei Wu 1, Yan Wang 1, Yan Xia 2, Yong-Yuan Jiang 1, Jie Song 1,3,4,5. We propose a superconducting qutrit-resonator chain model, and analytically work out forms of its topological edge states. The existence of the zero-energy mode enables to generate a state transfer between two ends of the chain, accompanied with state flips of all intermediate qutrits, based on which N N -body Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states can be generated with great robustness against disorders of coupling strengths.

title: GuiltyWalker: Distance to illicit nodes in the Bitcoin network Conference: KDD ’21; August 14–18, 2021; Singapore Workshop on Machine Learning in Finance (KDD ’21), August, 2021, Singapore CCS: Computing methodologies Supervised learning by classification
creator: Catarina Oliveira, João Torres, Maria Inês Silva, David Aparício, João Tiago Ascensão, Pedro Bizarro
description: Abstract . Money laundering is a global phenomenon with wide-reaching social and economic consequences. Cryptocurrencies are particularly susceptible due to the lack of control by authorities and their anonymity. Thus, it is important to develop new techniques to detect and prevent illicit cryptocurrency transactions.

title: Quantum and Semiquantum Pseudometrics and applications
creator: François Golse, Thierry Paul
description: Abstract . We establish a Kantorovich duality for he pseudometric ℰ ℏ \mathcal{E}_{\hbar} introduced in [F. Golse, T. Paul, Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 223 (2017), 57–94], obtained from the usual Monge-Kantorovich distance dist MK , 2 \operatorname{dist_{MK,2}} between classical densities by quantization of one side of the two densities involved.

title: Singlino-dominated dark matter in general NMSSM
creator: Junjie Cao, Demin Li, Jingwei Lian, Yuanfang Yue, Haijing Zhou
description: Abstract The general Next-to-Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (NMSSM) describes the singlino-dominated dark-matter (DM) property by four independent parameters: singlet-doublet Higgs coupling coefficient λ \lambda , Higgsino mass μ t ​ o ​ t \mu_{tot} , DM mass m χ ~ 1 0 m_{\tilde{\chi}_{1}^{0}} , and singlet Higgs self-coupling coefficient κ \kappa .

title: Enhancing Reading Strategies by Exploring A Theme-based Approach to Literature Surveys Volume: 40 Issue: 3
creator: T. Howden 1 , P. Le Bras 1 , T. S. Methven 2 , S. Padilla 1 , and M. J. Chantler 1 1 School of Mathematical and Computer Sciences, Heriot-Watt University, Edinburgh, United Kingdom 2 School of Computing, Edinburgh Napier University, Edinburgh, United Kingdom
description: Abstract Searching large digital repositories can be extremely frustrating, as common list-based formats encourage users to adopt a convenience-sampling approach that favours chance discovery and random search, over meaningful exploration. We have designed a methodology that allows users to visually and thematically explore corpora, while developing personalised holistic reading strategies.

title: Electronic localization in small-angle twisted bilayer graphene
creator: V. Hung Nguyen 1, D. Paszko 1 , M. Lamparski 2 , B. Van Troeye 2 , V. Meunier 2 , and J.-C. Charlier 1
description: Abstract Close to a magical angle, twisted bilayer graphene (TBLG) systems exhibit isolated flat electronic bands and, accordingly, strong electron localization. TBLGs have hence been ideal platforms to explore superconductivity, correlated insulating states, magnetism, and quantized anomalous Hall states in reduced dimension. Below a threshold twist angle ( ∼ \sim 1.1 ∘ 1.

title: Differential Entropy Rate Characterisations of Long Range Dependent Processes
creator: Andrew Feutrill, Matthew Roughan
description: Abstract A quantity of interest to characterise continuous-valued stochastic processes is the differential entropy rate. The rate of convergence of many properties of long range dependent (LRD) processes is slower than might be expected, based on the intuition for conventional processes, e.g. Markov processes . Is this also true of the entropy rate?

title: Can the nature of a 0 ​ ( 980 ) a_{0}(980) be tested in the D s + → π + ​ π 0 ​ η D_{s}^{+}\to\pi^{+}\pi^{0}\eta decay?
creator: Xi-Zhe Ling, Ming-Zhu Liu, Jun-Xu Lu, Li-Sheng Geng, Ju-Jun Xie
description: Abstract From the amplitude analysis of the D s + → π + ​ π 0 ​ η D^{+}_{s}\to\pi^{+}\pi^{0}\eta decay, the BESIII Collaboration firstly observed the D s + → a 0 ​ ( 980 ) + ​ π 0 D^{+}_{s}\to a_{0}(980)^{+}\pi^{0} and D s + → a 0 ​ ( 980 ) 0 ​ π + D^{+}_{s}\to a_{0}(980)^{0}\pi^{+} decay

title: Some observations and speculations on partitions into d d -th powers Thanks: The research of the author is supported by the grant of the National Science Centre (NCN), Poland, no. UMO-2019/34/E/ST1/00094
creator: Maciej Ulas
description: Abstract . The aim of this note is to provoke discussion concerning arithmetic properties of function p d ​ ( n ) p_{d}(n) counting partitions of an positive integer n n into d d -th powers, where d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 .

title: Topological phases in N- layer ABC- graphene boron-nitride moire superlattices
creator: David Andrés Galeano González, Bheema Lingam Chittari, Youngju Park, Jin-Hua Sun, Jeil Jung
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by David Andrés Galeano González, Bheema Lingam Chittari, Youngju Park, Jin-Hua Sun, Jeil Jung. Rhombohedral N = 3 N=3 trilayer graphene on hexagonal boron nitride (TLG/BN) hosts gate-tunable, valley-contrasting, nearly flat topological bands that can trigger spontaneous quantum Hall phases under appropriate conditions of the valley and spin polarization. Recent experiments have shown signatures of C = 2 valley Chern bands at 1/4 hole filling, in contrast to the predicted value of C = 3.

title: Intelligent Reflecting Surface-assisted MU-MISO Systems with Imperfect Hardware: Channel Estimation and Beamforming Design
creator: Anastasios Papazafeiropoulos, Cunhua Pan, Pandelis Kourtessis, Symeon Chatzinotas, John M. Senior
description: Abstract Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS), consisting of low-cost passive elements, is a promising technology for improving the spectral and energy efficiency of the fifth-generation (5G) and beyond networks. It is also noteworthy that an IRS can shape the reflected signal propagation.

title: Approximation of weak geodesics and subharmonicity of Mabuchi energy, II: ε \varepsilon -geodesics
creator: Long Li
description: Abstract . The purpose of this article is to study the strict convexity of the Mabuchi functional along a 𝒞 1 , 1 ¯ {\mathcal{C}}^{1,\bar{1}} -geodesic, with the aid of the ε \varepsilon -geodesics. We proved the L 2 L^{2} -convergence of the fiberwise volume element of the ε \varepsilon -geodesic.

title: Error Convergence Analysis and Stability of a Cloud Control AGV
creator: Shreya Tayade 1 , Peter Rost 2 and Andreas Maeder 2
description: Abstract In this paper, we present a cloud based Automated Guided vehicle (AGV) control system. A controller in an Edge cloud sends the control inputs to an AGV to follow a predefined reference track over a wireless channel. The AGV feedback the position update via uplink channel.

title: Imprinting tunable π \pi -magnetism in graphene nanoribbons via edge extensions
creator: Michele Pizzochero, Efthimios Kaxiras
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Michele Pizzochero, Efthimios Kaxiras. Magnetic carbon nanostructures are currently under scrutiny for a wide spectrum of applications. Here, we theoretically investigate armchair graphene nanoribbons patterned with asymmetric edge extensions consisting of laterally fused naphtho groups, as recently fabricated via on-surface synthesis. We show that an individual edge extension acts as a spin- 1 2 \frac{1}{2} center and develops a sizable spin-polarization of the conductance around the band edges.

title: Detecting the flavor content of the vacuum using the Dirac operator spectrum
creator: Jian Liang, Andrei Alexandru, Yu-Jiang Bi, Terrence Draper, Keh-Fei Liu, Yi-Bo Yang, χ \chi QCD Collaboration
description: Abstract We compute the overlap Dirac spectrum on three gauge ensembles generated using 2 + 1 2+1 -flavor domain wall fermions. The three ensembles have different lattice spacings and two of them have quark masses tuned to the physical point. The spectral density is determined up to λ ∼ \lambda\sim 100 MeV with subpercentage statistical uncertainty.

title: Assignments of the Y ⁡ ( 2040 ) Y(2040) , ρ ⁡ ( 1900 ) \rho(1900) , and ρ ⁡ ( 2150 ) \rho(2150) in the quark model
creator: Zheng-Ya Li, De-Min Li, En Wang, Wen-Cheng Yan, Qin-Tao Song
description: Abstract Recently, the BESIII Collaboration reported a resonance Y ⁡ ( 2040 ) Y(2040) with M = 2034 ± 13 ± 9 M=2034\pm 13\pm 9 MeV and Γ = 234 ± 30 ± 25 \Gamma=234\pm 30\pm 25 MeV in the process of e + ​ e − → ω ​ π 0 e^{+}e^{-}\rightarrow\omega\pi^{0} .

title: Cutoff phenomenon of the Glauber dynamics for the Ising model on complete multipartite graphs in the high temperature regime
creator: Heejune Kim
description: Abstract . In this paper, the Glauber dynamics for the Ising model on the complete multipartite graph K n ​ p 1 , … , n ​ p m K_{np_{1},\dots,np_{m}} is investigated where 0 < p i < 1 0<p_{i}<1 is the proportion of the vertices in the i i th component.

title: Geometric signatures of tissue surface tension in a three-dimensional model of confluent tissue
creator: Preeti Sahu 1,2,∗ , J. M. Schwarz 1,3 and M. Lisa Manning 1,
description: Abstract In dense biological tissues, cell types performing different roles remain segregated by maintaining sharp interfaces. To better understand the mechanisms for such sharp compartmentalization, we study the effect of an imposed heterotypic tension at the interface between two distinct cell types in a fully 3D model for confluent tissues.

title: Average fidelity and fidelity deviation in noisy quantum teleportation
creator: Wooyeong Song, Junghee Ryu, Kyunghyun Baek, Jeongho Bang
description: Abstract We analyze the average fidelity (say, F F ) and the fidelity deviation (say, D D ) in noisy-channel quantum teleportation. Here, F F represents how well teleportation is performed on average and D D quantifies whether the teleportation is performed impartially on the given inputs, that is, the condition of universality.

title: Weak-lensing Mass Reconstruction of Galaxy Clusters with Convolutional Neural Network Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , Keras ( Chollet et al. 2015 ) , Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , NumPy/SciPy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 ) , Pandas ( McKinney 2010 ) , SExtractor ( Bertin & Arnouts 1996 ) ,
creator: Sungwook E. Hong (홍성욱), Sangnam Park, M. James Jee, Dongsu Bak, Sangjun Cha
description: Abstract We introduce a novel method for reconstructing the projected matter distributions of galaxy clusters with weak-lensing (WL) data based on convolutional neural network (CNN). Training datasets are generated with ray-tracing through cosmological simulations. We control the noise level of the galaxy shear catalog such that it mimics the typical properties of the existing ground-based WL observations of galaxy clusters.

title: Dynamic susceptibilities in dense soft athermal spheres under a finite-rate shear
creator: Norihiro Oyama, Takeshi Kawasaki, Kuniyasu Saitoh
description: Abstract The mechanical responses of dense packings of soft athermal spheres under a finite-rate shear are studied by means of molecular dynamics simulations. We investigate the volume fraction and shear rate dependence of the fluctuations in the shear stress and the interparticle contact number.
