A rooted tree 𝒯 \mathcal{T} with leaf-set S ⊂ [ n ] S\subset[n] is induced by S S in T T if 𝒯 \mathcal{T} is the lowest common ancestor subtree for S S , with all its degree-2 vertices suppressed.

title: Adversarial Poisoning Attacks and Defense for General Multi-Class Models Based On Synthetic Reduced Nearest Neighbors
creator: Pooya Tavallali University of California, Merced ptavallali@ucmerced.edu, Vahid Behzadan Tagliatela College of Engineering University of New Haven vbehzadan@newhaven.edu, Peyman Tavallali Independent Researcher tavallali@gmail.com, Mukesh Singhal University of California, Merced msinghal@ucmerced.ed
description: Abstract State-of-the-art machine learning models are vulnerable to data poisoning attacks whose purpose is to undermine the integrity of the model. However, the current literature on data poisoning attacks is mainly focused on ad hoc techniques that are only applicable to specific machine learning models.

title: Approximation Algorithms for Generalized Multidimensional Knapsack
creator: Arindam Khan, Eklavya Sharma K. V. N. Sreenivas
description: Abstract We study a generalization of the knapsack problem with geometric and vector constraints. The input is a set of rectangular items, each with an associated profit and d d nonnegative weights ( d d -dimensional vector), and a square knapsack.

title: Spin and polarization effects on the nonlinear Breit-Wheeler pair production in laser-plasma interaction
creator: Huai-Hang Song, Wei-Min Wang, Yan-Fei Li, Bing-Jun Li, Yu-Tong Li, Zheng-Ming Sheng, Li-Ming Chen, Jie Zhang
description: Abstract The spin effect of electrons/positrons ( e − e^{-} / e + e^{+} ) and polarization effect of γ \gamma photons are investigated in the interaction of two counter-propagating linearly polarized 10-PW-class laser pulses with a thin foil target.

title: Higher-order generalized- α \alpha methods for parabolic problems Journal: Arxiv
creator: Pouria Behnoudfar, Quanling Deng, Victor M. Calo
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pouria Behnoudfar, Quanling Deng, Victor M. Calo. We propose a new class of high-order time-marching schemes with dissipation user-control and unconditional stability for parabolic equations. High-order time integrators can deliver the optimal performance of highly-accurate and robust spatial discretizations such as isogeometric analysis. The generalized- α \alpha method delivers unconditional stability and second-order accuracy in time and controls the numerical dissipation in the discrete spectrum’s high-frequency region.

title: Pairing and the spin susceptibility of the polarized unitary Fermi gas in the normal phase
creator: Lukas Rammelmüller, Yaqi Hou, Joaquín E. Drut, Jens Braun
description: Abstract We theoretically study the pairing behavior of the unitary Fermi gas in the normal phase. Our analysis is based on the static spin susceptibility, which characterizes the response to an external magnetic field. We obtain this quantity by means of the complex Langevin approach and compare our calculations to available literature data in the spin-balanced case.

title: Contribution of collapsars, supernovae, and neutron star mergers to the evolution of r-process elements in the Galaxy
creator: Yuta Yamazaki 1,2, Toshitaka Kajino 1,2,3, Grant J. Mathews 2,4, Xiaodong Tang 5, Jianrong Shi 6, Michael A. Famiano 2,7
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yuta Yamazaki 1,2, Toshitaka Kajino 1,2,3, Grant J. Mathews 2,4, Xiaodong Tang 5, Jianrong Shi 6, Michael A. Famiano 2,7. We study the evolution of rapid neutron-capture process (r-process) isotopes in the Galaxy. We analyze relative contributions from core collapse supernovae (CCSNe), neutron star mergers (NSMs) and collapsars under a range of astrophysical conditions and nuclear input data.

title: Toward Improving Coherence and Diversity of Slogan Generation
creator: Yiping Jin 1, Akshay Bhatia 2, Dittaya Wanvarie 1,∗, Phu T. V. Le 2
description: Abstract Previous work in slogan generation focused on utilising slogan skeletons mined from existing slogans. While some generated slogans can be catchy, they are often not coherent with the company’s focus or style across their marketing communications because the skeletons are mined from other companies’ slogans.

title: ALMA Observations of the Asymmetric Dust Disk around DM Tau
creator: Jun Hashimoto, Takayuki Muto, Ruobing Dong, Hauyu Baobab Liu, Nienke van der Marel, Logan Francis, Yasuhiro Hasegawa, Takashi Tsukagoshi
description: Abstract We report an analysis of the dust disk around DM Tau, newly observed with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 1.3 mm. The ALMA observations with high sensitivity (8.4 μ \mu Jy/beam) and high angular resolution (35 mas, 5.1 au) detect two asymmetries on the ring at r ∼ r\sim 20 au.

title: On the strong convergence of a perturbed algorithm to the unique solution of a variational inequality problem
creator: Ramzi May, Zahrah BinAli
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ramzi May, Zahrah BinAli. Let Q Q be a nonempty closed and convex subset of a real Hilbert space ℋ \mathscr{H} . T : Q → Q T:Q\rightarrow Q is a nonexpansive mapping which has a least one fixed point. f : Q → ℋ f:Q\rightarrow\mathscr{H} is a Lipschitzian function, and F : Q → ℋ F:Q\rightarrow\mathscr{H} is a Lipschitzian and strongly monotone mapping.

title: Theoretical and Experimental Perspectives of Quantum Verification
creator: Jose Carrasco, Andreas Elben, Christian Kokail, Barbara Kraus, Peter Zoller
description: Abstract In this perspective we discuss verification of quantum devices in the context of specific examples, formulated as proposed experiments. Our first example is verification of analog quantum simulators as Hamiltonian learning, where the input Hamiltonian as design goal is compared with the parent Hamiltonian for the quantum states prepared on the device.

title: Strongly topological gyrogroups and quotient with respect to L L -subgyrogroups Thanks: The authors are supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (Nos. 11661057, 12071199) and the Natural Science Foundation of Jiangxi Province, China (No. 20192ACBL20045) *corresponding author
creator: Meng Bao, Xuewei Ling, Xiaoquan Xu*
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Meng Bao, Xuewei Ling, Xiaoquan Xu*. In this paper, some generalized metric properties in strongly topological gyrogroups are studied. In particular, it is proved that when G G is a strongly topological gyrogroup with a symmetric neighborhood base 𝒰 \mathscr{U} at 0 0 and H H is a second-countable admissible subgyrogroup generated from 𝒰 \mathscr{U} , if the quotient space G / H G/H is an ℵ 0 \aleph_{0} -space (resp., cosmic space), then G G is also an ℵ 0 \aleph_{0} -space (resp.,

title: Spectrum of the doubly charmed molecular pentaquarks in chiral effective field theory
creator: Kan Chen 1,2, Bo Wang 1,2, Shi-Lin Zhu 1,2
description: Abstract We perform a systematic study on the interactions of the Σ c ( ∗ ) ​ D ( ∗ ) \Sigma_{c}^{(*)}D^{(*)} systems within the framework of chiral effective field theory. We introduce the contact term, one-pion-exchange and two-pion-exchange contributions to describe the short-, long-, and intermediate-range interactions.

title: Performance of nonconforming spectral element method for Stokes problems
creator: N. Kishore Kumar, Shubhashree Mohapatra
description: Abstract In this paper, we study the performance of the non-conforming least-squares spectral element method for Stokes problem. Generalized Stokes problem has been considered and the method is shown to be exponential accurate. The numerical method is nonconforming and higher order spectral element functions are used. The same order spectral element functions are used for both velocity and pressure variables.

title: Vorticity Production at Fluid Interfaces in Two-dimensional Flows
creator: Maurice Rossi 1,2, Daniel Fuster 1,2
description: Abstract This work revisits the production of vorticity at an interface separating two immiscible incompressible fluids. A new decomposition of the vorticity flux is proposed in a two-dimensional context which allows to compute explicitly such a quantity in terms of surface tension σ \sigma , viscosity μ \mu and gravity g g .

title: Assessment of intra-tumor heterogeneity in a two-dimensional vascular tumor growth model Publication type: Article Type
creator: Ioannis Lampropoulos, Michail Kavousanakis*
description: Abstract We present a two-dimensional continuum model of tumor growth, which treats the tissue as a composition of six distinct fluid phases; their dynamics are governed by the equations of mass and momentum conservation. Our model divides the cancer cells phase into two sub-phases depending on their maturity state.

title: Novel multi-step predictor-corrector schemes for backward stochastic differential equations
creator: Qiang Han, Shaolin Ji
description: Abstract Abstract . Novel multi-step predictor-corrector numerical schemes have been derived for approximating decoupled forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs). The stability and high order rate of convergence of the schemes are rigorously proved. We also present a sufficient and necessary condition for the stability of the schemes.

title: Exact variational dynamics of the multi-mode Bose-Hubbard model based on SU( M M ) coherent states
creator: Yulong Qiao, Frank Grossmann
description: Abstract We propose a variational approach to the dynamics of the Bose-Hubbard model beyond the mean field approximation. To develop a numerical scheme, we use a discrete overcomplete set of Glauber coherent states and its connection to the generalized coherent states studied in depth by Perelomov [A. Perelomov, Generalized Coherent States and Their Applications , Springer-Verlag (Berlin, 1986)].

title: A formal proof of modal completeness for provability logic
creator: Marco Maggesi, Cosimo Perini Brogi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Marco Maggesi, Cosimo Perini Brogi. This work presents a formalized proof of modal completeness for Gödel-Löb provability logic (GL) in the HOL Light theorem prover. We describe the code we developed, and discuss some details of our implementation, focusing on our choices in structuring proofs which make essential use of the tools of HOL Light and which differ in part from the standard strategies found in main textbooks covering the topic in an informal setting.

title: Refinements and Symmetries of the Morris identity for volumes of flow polytopes Thanks: August 9, 2026 Thanks: ⋆ Department of Mathematics and Statistics, UMass, Amherst, MA 01003. Email: ahmorales@math.umass.edu Thanks: † Northview High School, Johns Creek, GA 30097. Email: williamshi080@gmail.com
creator: Alejandro H. Morales ⋆ , and William Shi †
description: Abstract . Flow polytopes are an important class of polytopes in combinatorics whose lattice points and volumes have interesting properties and relations. The Chan–Robbins–Yuen (CRY) polytope is a flow polytope with normalized volume equal to the product of consecutive Catalan numbers. Zeilberger proved this by evaluating the Morris constant term identity, but no combinatorial proof is known.

title: Divergence-conforming methods for transient doubly-diffusive flows: A priori and a posteriori error analysis Thanks: This work has been supported by ANID (Chile) through Fondecyt project 1210610, CMM, project ANID/PIA/AFB170001, and CRHIAM, project ANID/FONDAP/15130015; by the Sponsored Research & I
creator: Raimund Bürger, Arbaz Khan, Paul E. Méndez, Ricardo Ruiz-Baier
description: Abstract . The analysis of the double-diffusion model and 𝐇 ⁡ ( div ) \mathbf{H}(\mathrm{div}) -conforming method introduced in [Bürger, Méndez, Ruiz-Baier, SINUM (2019), 57:1318–1343] is extended to the time-dependent case. In addition, the efficiency and reliability analysis of residual-based a posteriori error estimators for the steady, semi-discrete, and fully discrete problems is established.

title: Universal algebra in UniMath
creator: Gianluca Amato, Matteo Calosci, Marco Maggesi, Cosimo Perini Brogi
description: Abstract We present our library for Universal Algebra in the UniMath framework dealing with multi-sorted signatures, their algebras, and the basics for equation systems. We show how to implement term algebras over a signature without resorting to general inductive constructions (currently not allowed in UniMath) still retaining the computational nature of the definition.

title: On high-dimensional wavelet eigenanalysis Thanks: H.W. was partially supported by ANR-18-CE45-0007 MUTATION, France. G.D.’s long term visits to ENS de Lyon were supported by the school, the CNRS, the Carol Lavin Bernick faculty grant and the Simons Foundation collaboration grant # ​ 714014 \#714014
creator: Patrice Abry, B. Cooper Boniece, Gustavo Didier, Herwig Wendt
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Patrice Abry, B. Cooper Boniece, Gustavo Didier, Herwig Wendt. In this paper, we characterize the asymptotic and large scale behavior of the eigenvalues of wavelet random matrices in high dimensions. We assume that possibly non-Gaussian, finite-variance p p -variate measurements are made of a low-dimensional r r -variate ( r ≪ p r\ll p ) fractional stochastic process with non-canonical scaling coordinates and in the presence of additive high-dimensional noise. The measurements are correlated both time-wise and between rows.

title: Almost Robinson geometries Thanks: Funding. AF was supported by GNSAGA of INdAM, by PRIN 2017 “Real and Complex Manifolds: Topology, Geometry and Holomorphic Dynamics" and by a grant from the Simons Foundation (#944448). TL was supported by the Australian Research Council (Discovery Program DP190102
creator: Anna Fino, Thomas Leistner, Arman Taghavi-Chabert ∗
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Anna Fino, Thomas Leistner, Arman Taghavi-Chabert ∗. We investigate the geometry of almost Robinson manifolds, Lorentzian analogues of almost Hermitian manifolds, defined by Nurowski and Trautman as Lorentzian manifolds of even dimension equipped with a totally null complex distribution of maximal rank. Associated to such a structure, there is a congruence of null curves, which, in dimension four, is geodesic and non-shearing if and only if the complex distribution is involutive.

title: Closed orbits of Reeb fields on Sasakian manifolds and elliptic curves on Vaisman manifolds
creator: Liviu Ornea
description: Abstract Abstract A compact complex manifold V is called Vaisman if it admits an Hermitian metric which is conformal to a Kähler one, and a non-isometric conformal action by \mathbb{C} . It is called quasi-regular if the \mathbb{C} -action has closed orbits. In this case the corresponding leaf space is a projective orbifold, called the quasi-regular quotient of V .

title: Dependence on beam energy and nuclear equation of state of anisotropic flow and particle production in low-energy heavy-ion collisions
creator: Sumit Kumar Kundu, Yoshini Bailung, Sudhir Pandurang Rode, Partha Pratim Bhaduri, Ankhi Roy
description: Abstract We analyse various flow coefficients of anisotropic momentum distribution of final state particles in mid-central ( b b = = 5–9 f ​ m fm ) Au + Au collisions in the beam energy range E Lab \rm E_{\rm Lab} = = 1 ​ A − 158 ​ A 1A-158A GeV.

title: Investigating Trade-offs in Utility, Fairness and Differential Privacy in Neural Networks
creator: Marlotte Pannekoek, Giacomo Spigler
description: Abstract To enable an ethical and legal use of machine learning algorithms, they must both be fair and protect the privacy of those whose data are being used. However, implementing privacy and fairness constraints might come at the cost of utility ( Jayaraman & Evans 2019 ; Gong et al. 2020 ) .

title: L-SNet: From region localization to scale invariant medical image segmentation
creator: Jiahao Xie, Sheng Zhang, Jianwei Lu, Ye Luo
description: Abstract Coarse-to-fine models and cascade segmentation architectures are widely adopted to solve the problem of large scale variations in medical image segmentation. However, those methods have two primary limitations: the first-stage segmentation becomes a performance bottleneck; the lack of overall differentiability makes the training process of two stages asynchronous and inconsistent.

title: An End-to-end Model for Entity-level Relation Extraction using Multi-instance Learning
creator: Markus Eberts Adrian Ulges
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Markus Eberts Adrian Ulges. We present a joint model for entity-level relation extraction from documents. In contrast to other approaches – which focus on local intra-sentence mention pairs and thus require annotations on mention level – our model operates on entity level. To do so, a multi-task approach is followed that builds upon coreference resolution and gathers relevant signals via multi-instance learning with multi-level representations combining global entity and local mention information.

title: Tunable Kondo resonance at a pristine two-dimensional Dirac semimetal on a Kondo insulator
creator: Jinwoong Hwang, Seungseok Lee, Ji-Eun Lee, Minhee Kang, Hyejin Ryu, Hyun-Jeong Joo, Jonathan Denlinger, Jae-Hoon Park, Choongyu Hwang
description: Abstract Proximity of two different materials leads to an intricate coupling of quasiparticles so that an unprecedented electronic state is often realized at the interface. Here, we demonstrate a resonance-type many-body ground state in graphene, a non-magnetic two-dimensional Dirac semimetal, when grown on SmB 6 , a Kondo insulator, via thermal decomposition of fullerene molecules.

title: Development of a Fully-Coupled Harmonic Balance Method and a Refined Energy Method for the Computation of Flutter-Induced Limit Cycle Oscillations of Bladed Disks with Nonlinear Friction Contacts Journal: JFS
creator: Christian Berthold, Johann Gross, Christian Frey, Malte Krack
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Christian Berthold, Johann Gross, Christian Frey, Malte Krack. Flutter stability is a dominant design constraint of modern gas and steam turbines. To further increase the feasible design space, flutter-tolerant designs are currently explored, which may undergo Limit Cycle Oscillations (LCOs) of acceptable, yet not vanishing, level. Bounded self-excited oscillations are a priori a nonlinear phenomenon, and can thus only be explained by nonlinear interactions such as dry stick-slip friction in mechanical joints.

title: Modeling 3D Surface Manifolds with a Locally Conditioned Atlas
creator: Przemysław Spurek, Sebastian Winczowski, Maciej Zięba, Tomasz Trzciński, Kacper Kania, Marcin Mazur
description: Abstract Recently proposed 3D object reconstruction methods represent a mesh with an atlas - a set of planar patches approximating the surface. However, their application in a real-world scenario is limited since the surfaces of reconstructed objects contain discontinuities, which degrades the quality of the final mesh.

title: Polynomial Approximations of Conditional Expectations in Scalar Gaussian Channels
creator: Wael Alghamdi, Flavio P. Calmon
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Wael Alghamdi, Flavio P. Calmon. We consider a channel Y = X + N Y=X+N where X X is a random variable satisfying 𝔼 ⁡ [ | X | ] < ∞ \mathbb{E}[|X|]<\infty and N N is an independent standard normal random variable.

title: BlockHammer: Preventing RowHammer at Low Cost by Blacklisting Rapidly-Accessed DRAM Rows
creator: A. Giray Yağlıkçı 1 Minesh Patel 1 Jeremie S. Kim 1 Roknoddin Azizi 1 Ataberk Olgun 1 Lois Orosa 1 Hasan Hassan 1 Jisung Park 1 Konstantinos Kanellopoulos 1 Taha Shahroodi 1 Saugata Ghose 2 Onur Mutlu 1 1 ETH Zürich 2 University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign
description: Abstract Aggressive memory density scaling causes modern DRAM devices to suffer from RowHammer, a phenomenon where rapidly activating (i.e., hammering) a DRAM row can cause bit-flips in physically-nearby rows. Recent studies demonstrate that modern DDR4/LPDDR4 DRAM chips, including chips previously marketed as RowHammer-safe, are even more vulnerable to RowHammer than older DDR3 DRAM chips.

title: The classification of Kleinian groups of Hausdorff dimensions at most one and Burnside’s conjecture
creator: Yong Hou
description: Abstract In this paper we provide the complete classification of convex cocompact Kleinian group of Hausdorff dimensions less than 1 . 1. In particular, we prove that every convex cocompact Kleinian group of Hausdorff dimension < 1 <1 is a classical Schottky group. This upper bound is sharp.

title: Robust Generalization and Safe Query-Specialization in Counterfactual Learning to Rank Conference: Proceedings of the Web Conference 2021; April 19–23, 2021; Ljubljana, Slovenia Proceedings of the Web Conference 2021 (WWW ’21), April 19–23, 2021, Ljubljana, Slovenia DOI: 10.1145/3442381.3450018 ISBN
creator: Harrie Oosterhuis, Maarten de Rijke
description: Abstract . Existing work in counterfactual LTR ( LTR ) has focussed on optimizing feature-based models that predict the optimal ranking based on document features. LTR methods based on bandit algorithms often optimize tabular models that memorize the optimal ranking per query. These types of model have their own advantages and disadvantages.

title: Impact of Graph Structures for QAOA on MaxCut
creator: Rebekah Herrman, Lorna Treffert, James Ostrowski, Phillip C. Lotshaw, Travis S. Humble, George Siopsis
description: Abstract The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is a promising method of solving combinatorial optimization problems using quantum computing. QAOA on the MaxCut problem has been studied extensively on specific families of graphs, however, little is known about the algorithm on arbitrary graphs.

title: Darboux families and the classification of real four-dimensional indecomposable coboundary Lie bialgebras
creator: J. de Lucas, D. Wysocki
description: Abstract This work introduces a new concept, the so-called Darboux family , which is employed to determine, to analyse geometrically, and to classify up to Lie algebra automorphisms, in a relatively easy manner, coboundary Lie bialgebras on real four-dimensional indecomposable Lie algebras. The Darboux family notion can be considered as a generalisation of the Darboux polynomial for a vector field.

title: Non-thermal radio supernova remnants of exiled Wolf-Rayet stars
creator: D. M.-A. Meyer, M. Pohl, M. Petrov, L. Oskinova
description: Abstract A signification fraction of Galactic massive stars ( ≥ 8 ​ M ⊙ \geq 8\,\rm M_{\odot} ) are ejected from their parent cluster and supersonically sail away through the interstellar medium (ISM). The winds of these fast-moving stars blow asymmetric bubbles thus creating a circumstellar environment in which stars eventually die with a supernova explosion.

title: On Forward Sufficient Dimension Reduction for Categorical and Ordinal Responses
creator: Harris Quach, Bing Li
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Harris Quach, Bing Li. We introduce a forward sufficient dimension reduction method for categorical or ordinal responses by extending the outer product of gradients and minimum average variance estimator to categorical and ordinal-categorical generalized linear models. Previous works in this direction extend forward regression to binary responses, and are applied in a pairwise manner for multi-category data, which is less efficient than our approach.

title: Cross-Domain Multi-Task Learning for Sequential Sentence Classification in Research Papers DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX CCS: Computing methodologies Information extraction CCS: Computing methodologies Multi-task learning CCS: Information systems Summarization CCS: Applied computing Document analysis CCS: Co
creator: Arthur Brack, Anett Hoppe, Pascal Buschermöhle, Ralph Ewerth
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Arthur Brack, Anett Hoppe, Pascal Buschermöhle, Ralph Ewerth. Sequential sentence classification deals with the categorisation of sentences based on their content and context. Applied to scientific texts, it enables the automatic structuring of research papers and the improvement of academic search engines. However, previous work has not investigated the potential of transfer learning for sentence classification across different scientific domains and the issue of different text structure of full papers and abstracts.

title: Full waveform inversion using extended and simultaneous sources Thanks: Corresponding author: Eran Treister.
creator: Sagi Buchatsky and Eran Treister
description: Abstract PDE-constrained optimization problems are often treated using the reduced formulation where the PDE constraints are eliminated. This approach is known to be more computationally feasible than other alternatives at large scales. However, the elimination of the constraints forces the optimization process to fulfill the constraints at all times.

title: Mathias and Silver forcing parametrized by density
creator: Giorgio Laguzzi, Heike Mildenberger, Brendan Stuber-Rousselle
description: Abstract . We define and investigate versions of Silver and Mathias forcing with respect to lower and upper density. We focus on properness, Axiom A, chain conditions, preservation of cardinals and adding Cohen reals. We find rough forcings that collapse 2 ω 2^{\omega} to ω \omega , while others are surprisingly gentle.

title: Analysing the Requirements for an Open Research Knowledge Graph: Use Cases, Quality Requirements and Construction Strategies
creator: Arthur Brack 1,2, Anett Hoppe 1, Markus Stocker 1, Sören Auer 1,2, Ralph Ewerth 1,2
description: Abstract Current science communication has a number of drawbacks and bottlenecks which have been subject of discussion lately: Among others, the rising number of published articles makes it nearly impossible to get a full overview of the state of the art in a certain field, or reproducibility is hampered by fixed-length, document-based publications which normally cannot cover all details of

title: Symplectic analysis for the Holst action with Dirac fields
creator: Mariniel Galvão
description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mariniel Galvão. I
Abstract

In this work we review the canonical analysis of the Holst-Dirac action from the point of view of the Faddeev-Jackiw symplectic procedure using the Barcelo Neto-Wotzasek algorithm. We replicate the results found in the literature for the theory’s constraints, recover some of the expressions for gauge symmetries of the main fields and perform the counting of the degrees of freedom.

title: Making Paper Reviewing Robust to Bid Manipulation Attacks
creator: Ruihan Wu, Chuan Guo, Felix Wu, Rahul Kidambi, Laurens van der Maaten, Kilian Q. Weinberger
description: Abstract Most computer science conferences rely on paper bidding to assign reviewers to papers. Although paper bidding enables high-quality assignments in days of unprecedented submission numbers, it also opens the door for dishonest reviewers to adversarially influence paper reviewing assignments.

title: STUaNet: Understanding uncertainty in spatiotemporal collective human mobility Conference: Proceedings of the Web Conference 2021; April 19–23, 2021; Ljubljana, Slovenia Proceedings of the Web Conference 2021 (WWW ’21), April 19–23, 2021, Ljubljana, Slovenia CCS: Information systems Web applications
creator: Zhengyang Zhou, Yang Wang, Xike Xie, Lei Qiao, Yuantao Li
description: Abstract . The high dynamics and heterogeneous interactions in the complicated urban systems have raised the issue of uncertainty quantification in spatiotemporal human mobility, to support critical decision-makings in risk-aware web applications such as urban event prediction where fluctuations are of significant interests.

title: Speech enhancement with mixture of deep experts with clean clustering pre-training
creator: Shlomo E. Chazan, Jacob Goldberger, Sharon Gannot
description: Abstract In this study we present a MoDE ( MoDE ) neural-network architecture for single microphone speech enhancement. Our architecture comprises a set of DNN , each of which is an ‘expert’ in a different speech spectral pattern such as phoneme.

title: Two Component Doublet-Triplet Scalar Dark Matter stabilising the Electroweak vacuum
creator: Nabarun Chakrabarty, Rishav Roshan, Arunansu Sil
description: Abstract A two component scalar dark matter scenario comprising an additional scalar doublet and a Y Y = 0 scalar triplet is proposed. Key features of the ensuing dark matter phenomenology are highlighted with emphasis on inter-conversion between the two dark matter components.

title: Validation Obligations: A Novel Approach to Check Compliance between Requirements and their Formal Specification
creator: 1 st Atif Mashkoor, 2 nd Michael Leuschel, 3 rd Alexander Egyed
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by 1 st Atif Mashkoor, 2 nd Michael Leuschel, 3 rd Alexander Egyed. Traditionally, practitioners use formal methods predominately for one half of the quality-assurance process: verification (do we build the software right?). The other half – validation (do we build the right software?) – has been given comparatively little attention.

title: Global multivariate model learning from hierarchically correlated data
creator: Edwin Rodríguez Horta, Alejandro Lage, Martin Weigt, Pierre Barrat-Charlaix
description: Abstract Inverse statistical physics aims at inferring models compatible with a set of empirical averages estimated from a high-dimensional dataset of independently distributed equilibrium configurations of a given system. However, in several applications such as biology, data result from stochastic evolutionary processes, and configurations are related through a hierarchical structure, typically represented by a tree, and therefore not independent.

title: Exact Algorithms for Scheduling Problems on Parallel Identical Machines with Conflict Jobs
creator: Minh Hoàng Hà, Dinh Quy Ta, Trung Thanh Nguyen*
description: Abstract Machine scheduling problems involving conflict jobs can be seen as a constrained version of the classical scheduling problem, in which some jobs are conflict in the sense that they cannot be proceeded simultaneously on different machines. This conflict constraint naturally arises in several practical applications and has recently received considerable attentions in the research community.

title: Multiple solutions for two classes of quasilinear problems defined on a nonreflexive Orlicz-Sobolev space Thanks: C. O. Alves was partially supported by CNPq/Brazil 304804/2017-7
creator: Claudianor O. Alves, Sabri Bahrouni and Marcos L. M. Carvalho
description: Abstract . In this paper we prove the existence and multiplicity of solutions for a large class of quasilinear problems on a nonreflexive Orlicz-Sobolev space. Here, we use the variational methods developed by Szulkin [ 32 ] combined with some properties of the weak ∗ topology. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 35A15, 35J62, 46E30 1.

title: Pion form factor and charge radius from Lattice QCD at physical point
creator: Xiang Gao, Nikhil Karthik, Swagato Mukherjee, Peter Petreczky, Sergey Syritsyn, Yong Zhao
description: Abstract We present our results on the electromagnetic form factor of pion over a wide range of Q 2 Q^{2} using lattice QCD simulations with Wilson-clover valence quarks and HISQ sea quarks. We study the form factor at the physical point with a lattice spacing a = 0.076 a=0.076 fm.

title: Artificial Intelligence based Autonomous Molecular Design for Medical Therapeutic: A Perspective Journal: ArXiv
creator: Rajendra P. Joshi, Neeraj Kumar ∗
description: Abstract Domain-aware machine learning (ML) models have been increasingly adopted for accelerating small molecule therapeutic design in the recent years. These models have been enabled by significant advancement in state-of-the-art artificial intelligence (AI) and computing infrastructures. Several ML architectures are predominantly and independently used either for predicting the properties of small molecules, or for generating lead therapeutic candidates.

title: TESS Hunt for Young and Maturing Exoplanets (THYME) IV: Three small planets orbiting a 120 Myr-old star in the Pisces–Eridanus stream sometimes called Meingast-1 Facilities: LCO, SALT, TESS, SOAR, PEST, WASP, LCO, Spitzer numpy Harris et al. 2020 , scipy Virtanen et al. 2020 , matplotlib Hunter 2007
creator: Elisabeth R. Newton, Andrew W. Mann, Adam L. Kraus, John H. Livingston, Andrew Vanderburg, Jason L. Curtis, Pa Chia Thao, Keith Hawkins, Mackenna L. Wood, Aaron C. Rizzuto, Abderahmane Soubkiou, Benjamin M. Tofflemire, George Zhou, Ian J. M. Crossfield, Logan A. Pearce, Karen A. Collins, Dennis M. C
description: Abstract Young exoplanets can offer insight into the evolution of planetary atmospheres, compositions, and architectures. We present the discovery of the young planetary system TOI 451 (TIC 257605131, Gaia DR2 4844691297067063424). TOI 451 is a member of the 120-Myr-old Pisces–Eridanus stream (Psc–Eri).

title: Causal mediation analysis: From simple to more robust strategies for estimation of marginal natural (in)direct effects \support This is the final version of the paper (version 4), to be published in Statistics Surveys volume 17 (2023), https://doi.org/10.1214/22-SS140 . The main changes from version
creator: Trang Quynh Nguyen, Elizabeth L. Ogburn, Ian Schmid, Elizabeth B. Sarker, Noah Greifer, Ina M. Koning, Elizabeth A. Stuart
description: Abstract This paper aims to provide practitioners of causal mediation analysis with a better understanding of estimation options. We take as inputs two familiar strategies (weighting and model-based prediction) and a simple way of combining them (weighted models), and show how a range of estimators can be generated, with different modeling requirements and robustness properties.

title: SLS (Single ℓ 1 \ell_{1} Selection): a new greedy algorithm with an ℓ 1 \ell_{1} -norm selection rule
creator: Ramzi Ben Mhenni, Sébastien Bourguignon, Jérôme Idier
description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a new greedy algorithm for sparse approximation, called SLS for Single ℓ 1 \ell_{1} Selection . SLS essentially consists of a greedy forward strategy, where the selection rule of a new component at each iteration is based on solving a least-squares optimization problem, penalized by the ℓ 1 \ell_{1} norm of the remaining variables.

title: Trinucleon form factors with relativistic multirank separable kernels Journal: Nuclear Physics A
creator: Serge Bondarenko, Valery Burov, Sergey Yurev
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Serge Bondarenko, Valery Burov, Sergey Yurev. This paper studies elastic electron-trinucleon scattering in the relativistic impulse approximation. The amplitudes for a trinucleon have been obtained by solving the relativistic generalization of the Faddeev equations with a multirank separable kernel of the nucleon-nucleon interactions. The static approximation and additional relativistic corrections for the trinucleon electromagnetic form factors have been calculated for the momentum transfer squared up to 50 fm -2 .

title: Peter Mészáros
description: Abstract Solid matter with zero shear modulus in flat universe Abstract For a perfect fluid, the quantity defined through mixed components of the stress-energy tensor \widetilde{w}=(T_{i}^{\phantom{i}i}/3)/(-T_{0}^{\phantom{0}0}) is independent on the choice of coordinates only for two values of the pressure to energy density ratio w=p/\rho : for radiation with w=1/3 , and for dark energy with w=-1 .

title: Stability and Horizon Formation during Dissipative Collapse
creator: Nolene F. Naidu †, Robert S. Bogadi ‡, Anand Kaisavelu ∗, Megan Govender ∗∗
description: Abstract We investigate the role played by density inhomogeneities and dissipation on the final outcome of collapse of a self-gravitating sphere. By imposing a perturbative scheme on the thermodynamical variables and gravitational potentials we track the evolution of the collapse process starting off with an initially static perfect fluid sphere which is shear-free.

title: Superresolving second-order correlation imaging using synthesized colored noise speckles
creator: Zheng Li ‡, Xiaoyu Nie ‡, Fan Yang ‡, Xiangpei Liu, Dongyu Liu, Xiaolong Dong, Xingchen Zhao, Tao Peng, M. Suhail Zubairy, Marlan O. Scully
description: Abstract 1 1 1 ‡ These authors contributed to this work equally. We present a novel method to synthesize non-trivial speckles that can enable superresolving second-order correlation imaging. The speckles acquire a unique anti-correlation in the spatial intensity fluctuation by introducing the blue noise spectrum to the input light fields through amplitude modulation.

title: Edge Deletion to Restrict the Size of an Epidemic
creator: Ajinkya Gaikwad, Soumen Maity
description: Abstract Given a graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) , a set ℱ \mathcal{F} of forbidden subgraphs, we study ℱ \mathcal{F} -Free Edge Deletion , where the goal is to remove a minimum number of edges such that the resulting graph does not contain any F ∈ ℱ F\in\mathcal{F} as a subgraph.

title: Slow and fast minimal speed traveling waves of the FKPP equation with chemotaxis
creator: Christopher Henderson
description: Abstract We examine a general model for the Fisher-KPP (FKPP) equation with nonlocal advection. The main interpretation of this model is as describing a diffusing and logistically growing population that is also influenced by intraspecific attraction or repulsion. For a particular choice of parameters, this specializes to the Keller-Segel-Fisher equation for chemotaxis.

title: On weakly 1 1 -absorbing prime ideals of commutative rings Thanks: Key Words : 1 1 -absorbing prime ideal, Weakly 1 1 -absorbing prime ideal, Prime ideal, Weakly prime ideal. Thanks: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification : 13A15, 13C05.
creator: M. J. Nikmehr, R. Nikandish and A. Yassine
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by M. J. Nikmehr, R. Nikandish and A. Yassine. Let R R be a commutative ring with identity. In this paper, we introduce the concept of weakly 1 1 -absorbing prime ideals which is a generalization of weakly prime ideals.

title: Bernstein-von Mises theorem for the Pitman-Yor process of nonnegative type
description: Abstract The Pitman-Yor process is a random probability distribution, that can be used as a prior distribution in a nonparametric Bayesian analysis. The process is of species sampling type and generates discrete distributions, which yield of the order n σ n^{\sigma} different values (“species”) in a random sample of size n n , if the type σ \sigma is positive.

title: ParaVS: A Simple, Fast, Efficient and Flexible Graph Neural Network Framework for Structure-Based Virtual Screening
creator: Junfeng Wu, Dawei Leng, Lurong Pan*
description: Abstract Structure-based virtual screening (SBVS) is a promising in silico technique that integrates computational methods into drug design. An extensively used method in SBVS is molecular docking. However, the docking process can hardly be computationally efficient and accurate simultaneously because classic mechanics scoring function is used to approximate, but hardly reach, the quantum mechanics precision in this method.

title: Temporal characterisation of silicon sensors on Timepix3 ASICs
creator: and P. Tsopelas
description: Abstract The timing performance of silicon sensors bump-bonded to Timepix3 ASICs is investigated, prior to and after different types of irradiation up to 8 × 10 15 ​ 1 ​ Me ​ V ​ n eq ​ cm − 2 8\times 10^{15}1\mathrm{\,Me\kern-1.00006ptV}\mathrm{\,n_{eq}}{\mathrm{\,cm}}^{-2} .

title: End-to-End Delay Guaranteed SFC Deployment: A Multi-level Mapping Approach Journal: Computer Communications
creator: Fatemeh Yaghoubpour, Bahador Bakhshi, Fateme Seifi
description: Abstract Network Function Virtualization (NFV) enables service providers to maximize the business profit via resource-efficient QoS provisioning for customer requested Service Function Chains (SFCs). In recent applications, end-to-end delay is one of the crucial QoS requirement needs to be guaranteed in SFC deployment.

title: Frequency Shift Algorithm: Application to a Frequency-Domain Multiplexing Readout of X-ray Transition-Edge Sensor Microcalorimeters
creator: D. Vaccaro, H. Akamatsu, J. van der Kuur, P. van der Hulst, A.C.T. Nieuwenhuizen, P. van Winden, L. Gottardi, R. den Hartog, M.P. Bruijn, M. D’Andrea, J.R. Gao, J.W.A. den Herder, R.W.M. Hoogeveen, B. Jackson, A.J. van der Linden, K. Nagayoshi, K. Ravensberg, M.L. Ridder, E. Taralli, M. de Wit
description: Abstract In the frequency-domain multiplexing (FDM) scheme, transition-edge sensors (TES) are individually coupled to superconducting LC filters and AC biased at MHz frequencies through a common readout line. To make efficient use of the available readout bandwidth and to minimize the effect of non-linearities, the LC resonators are usually designed to be on a regular grid.

title: Scattering states and bound states of exponential potentials
creator: Zafar Ahmed and H. F. Jones
description: Abstract We explore the relationships between scattering states and bound states of different non-analytic segments (depending on | x | |x| ) of the exponential potential, and elucidate the status of the special scattering states found in an earlier publication by Ahmed et al.

title: Effectively Testing System Configurations of Critical IoT Analytics Pipelines
creator: Morgan K. Geldenhuys 1 , Lauritz Thamsen 1 , Kain Kordian Gontarska 2 , Felix Lorenz 1 and Odej Kao 1
description: Abstract The emergence of the Internet of Things has seen the introduction of numerous connected devices used for the monitoring and control of even Critical Infrastructures. Distributed stream processing has become key to analyzing data generated by these connected devices and improving our ability to make decisions.

title: SWAGAN: A Style-based WAvelet-driven Generative Model
creator: Rinon Gal Tel-Aviv University, Dana Cohen Tel-Aviv University, Amit Bermano Tel-Aviv University, Daniel Cohen-Or Tel-Aviv University
description: Abstract In recent years, considerable progress has been made in the visual quality of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). Even so, these networks still suffer from degradation in quality for high-frequency content, stemming from a spectrally biased architecture, and similarly unfavorable loss functions.

title: The auto and cross angular power spectrum of the Cas A supernova remnant in radio and X-ray The auto and cross angular power spectrum of the Cas A supernova remnant in radio and X-ray – References 2021
creator: Preetha Saha, Somnath Bharadwaj, Susmita Chakravorty, Nirupam Roy, Samir Choudhuri, Hans Moritz Günther, Randall K. Smith
description: Abstract The shell type supernova remnant (SNR) Cas A exhibits structures at nearly all angular scales. Previous studies show the angular power spectrum ( C ℓ ) (C_{\ell}) of the radio emission to be a broken power law, consistent with MHD turbulence.

title: Hilbert Space Fragmentation and Exact Scars of Generalized Fredkin Spin Chains
creator: Christopher M. Langlett, Shenglong Xu
description: Abstract In this work, based on the Fredkin spin chain, we introduce a family of spin-1/2 many-body Hamiltonians with a three-site interaction featuring a fragmented Hilbert space with coexisting quantum many-body scars. The fragmentation results from an emergent kinetic constraint resembling the conserved spin configuration in the 1D Fermi-Hubbard model in the infinite onsite repulsion limit.

title: The Deepfake Detection Dilemma: A Multistakeholder Exploration of Adversarial Dynamics in Synthetic Media
creator: Claire Leibowicz, Sean McGregor, Aviv Ovadya
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Claire Leibowicz, Sean McGregor, Aviv Ovadya. Synthetic media detection technologies label media as either synthetic or non-synthetic and are increasingly used by journalists, web platforms, and the general public to identify misinformation and other forms of problematic content. As both well-resourced organizations and the non-technical general public generate more sophisticated synthetic media, the capacity for purveyors of problematic content to adapt induces a detection dilemma : as detection practices become more accessible, they become more easily circumvented.

title: Portable Real-Time Polarimeter: for Partially and Fully Polarized Light Journal: osajournal Publication type: Research Article
creator: Scott Wilkinson, \authormark 1 Aydan McKay, \authormark 1 Nicolas Braam, \authormark 1 Chris Secord, \authormark 2 Andrew MacRae, \authormark 1,*
description: Abstract We present a spinning waveplate polarimeter capable of producing real-time visualization of the polarization state of completely or partially polarized light. Our system utilizes a Raspberry Pi computer for a fully online, real-time analysis and visualization of the polarization state. This completely integrated approach provides an efficient tool for modern optics research labs and is well-suited for educational demonstrations.

title: District-Fair Participatory Budgeting
creator: D. Ellis Hershkowitz, Anson Kahng, Dominik Peters, Ariel D. Procaccia
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by D. Ellis Hershkowitz, Anson Kahng, Dominik Peters, Ariel D. Procaccia. Participatory budgeting is a method used by city governments to select public projects to fund based on residents’ votes. Many cities use participatory budgeting at a district level. Typically, a budget is divided among districts proportionally to their population, and each district holds an election over local projects and then uses its budget to fund the projects most preferred by its voters.

title: The effect of finite halo size on the clustering of neutral hydrogen
creator: and Stefano Camera
description: Abstract Post-reionisation 21cm intensity mapping experiments target the spectral line of neutral hydrogen (HI) resident in dark matter haloes. According to the halo model, these discrete haloes trace the continuous dark matter density field down to a certain scale, which is dependent on the halo physical size.

title: A Bayesian cohort component projection model to estimate adult populations at the subnational level in data-sparse settings
creator: Monica Alexander, Leontine Alkema
description: Abstract Accurate estimates of subnational populations are important for policy formulation and monitoring population health indicators. For example, estimates of the number of women of reproductive age are important to understand the population at risk to maternal mortality and unmet need for contraception.

title: Sequence-based Machine Learning Models in Jet Physics
creator: Rafael Teixeira de Lima
description: Abstract Sequence-based modeling broadly refers to algorithms that act on data that is represented as an ordered set of input elements. In particular, Machine Learning algorithms with sequences as inputs have seen successfull applications to important problems, such as Natural Language Processing (NLP) and speech signal modeling.

title: Baryon axial vector current in large- N c N_{c} chiral perturbation theory: Complete analysis for N c = 3 N_{c}=3
creator: Rubén Flores-Mendieta, Carlos Isaac García, Johann Hernández
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Rubén Flores-Mendieta, Carlos Isaac García, Johann Hernández. The baryon axial vector current is computed in heavy baryon chiral perturbation theory in the large- N c N_{c} limit, where N c N_{c} is the number of color charges.

title: A Novel Trick to Overcome the Phase Space Volume Change and the Use of Hamiltonian Trajectories with an emphasis on the Free Expansion
creator: P.D. Gujrati
description: Abstract We extend and successfully apply a recently proposed microstate nonequilibrium thermodynamics ( μ \mu NEQT) to study expansion/contraction processes. Here, the numbers of initial and final microstates { 𝔪 k } \left\{\mathfrak{m}_{k}\right\} are different so they cannot be connected by unique Hamiltonian trajectories.

title: Core Imaging Library – Part II: Multichannel reconstruction for dynamic and spectral tomography
creator: Evangelos Papoutsellis, Evelina Ametova, Claire Delplancke, Gemma Fardell, Jakob S. Jørgensen, Edoardo Pasca, Martin Turner, Ryan Warr, William R. B. Lionheart, Philip J. Withers
description: Abstract The newly developed Core Imaging Library (CIL) is a flexible plug and play library for tomographic imaging with a specific focus on iterative reconstruction. CIL provides building blocks for tailored regularised reconstruction algorithms and explicitly supports multichannel tomographic data. In the first part of this two-part publication, we introduced the fundamentals of CIL.

title: Nanoscale modification of WS 2 trion emission by its local electromagnetic environment
creator: Noémie Bonnet, Hae Yeon Lee, Fuhui Shao, Steffi Y. Woo, Jean-Denis Blazit, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Alberto Zobelli, Odile Stéphan, Mathieu Kociak, Silvija Gradecak-Garaj, Luiz H. G. Tizei
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Noémie Bonnet, Hae Yeon Lee, Fuhui Shao, Steffi Y. Woo, Jean-Denis Blazit, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Alberto Zobelli, Odile Stéphan, Mathieu Kociak, Silvija Gradecak-Garaj, Luiz H. G. Tizei. Structural, electronic, and chemical nanoscale modifications of transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers alter their optical properties, including the generation of single photon emitters.

title: Exponential suppression of bit or phase flip errors with repetitive error correction
creator: Google Quantum AI
description: Abstract Realizing the potential of quantum computing will require achieving sufficiently low logical error rates Preskill 2018 . Many applications call for error rates in the 10 − 15 10^{-15} regime Shor 1999 ; Fowler et al. 2012a ; Childs et al. 2018 ; Campbell et al. 2019 ; Kivlichan et al.

title: Pseudojump inversion in special r. b. Π 1 0 \Pi^{0}_{1} classes
creator: Hayden R. Jananthan
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hayden R. Jananthan. The Jump Inversion Theorem says that for every real A ≥ T 0 ′ A\geq_{\mathrm{T}}0^{\prime} there is a real B B such that A ≡ T B ′ ≡ T B ⊕ 0 ′ A\equiv_{\mathrm{T}}B^{\prime}\equiv_{\mathrm{T}}B\oplus 0^{\prime} . A known refinement of this theorem says that we can choose B B to be a member of any special Π 1 0 \Pi^{0}_{1} subclass of { 0 , 1 } ℕ \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}} .

title: Variational Bayesian sequence-to-sequence Networks for Memory-Efficient Sign Language Translation
creator: Harris Partaourides, Andreas Voskou, Dimitrios Kosmopoulos, Sotirios Chatzis, Dimitris N. Metaxas
description: Abstract Memory-efficient continuous Sign Language Translation is a significant challenge for the development of assisted technologies with real-time applicability for the deaf. In this work, we introduce a paradigm of designing recurrent deep networks whereby the output of the recurrent layer is derived from appropriate arguments from nonparametric statistics.

title: New insights into nuclear physics and weak mixing angle using electroweak probes
creator: M. Cadeddu, N. Cargioli, F. Dordei, C. Giunti, Y.F. Li, E. Picciau, C.A. Ternes, Y.Y. Zhang
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by M. Cadeddu, N. Cargioli, F. Dordei, C. Giunti, Y.F. Li, E. Picciau, C.A. Ternes, Y.Y. Zhang. Using the new results on coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering data in cesium-iodide provided by the COHERENT experiment, we determine a new measurement of the average neutron rms radius of Cs 133 {}^{133}\text{Cs} and I 127 {}^{127}\text{I} .

title: Personalized Embedding-based e-Commerce Recommendations at eBay CCS: Computing methodologies Learning from implicit feedback CCS: Information systems Personalization CCS: Information systems Information retrieval CCS: Information systems Recommender systems CCS: Computing methodologies Neural networ
creator: Tian Wang, Yuri M. Brovman, Sriganesh Madhvanath
description: Abstract . Recommender systems are an essential component of e-commerce marketplaces, helping consumers navigate massive amounts of inventory and find what they need or love. In this paper, we present an approach for generating personalized item recommendations in an e-commerce marketplace by learning to embed items and users in the same vector space.

title: Reconstruction of the dark sectors’ interaction: A model-independent inference and forecast from GW standard sirens 2022 Reconstruction of the dark sectors’ interaction: A model-independent inference and forecast from GW standard sirens – A
creator: Alexander Bonilla, Suresh Kumar, Rafael C. Nunes, Supriya Pan
description: Abstract Interacting dark matter (DM) - dark energy (DE) models have been intensively investigated in the literature for their ability to fit various data sets as well as to explain some observational tensions persisting within the Λ \Lambda CDM cosmology.

title: EvoSplit: An evolutionary approach to split a multi-label data set into disjoint subsets
creator: Francisco Florez-Revuelta
description: Abstract This paper presents a new evolutionary approach, EvoSplit, for the distribution of multi-label data sets into disjoint subsets for supervised machine learning. Currently, data set providers either divide a data set randomly or using iterative stratification, a method that aims to maintain the label (or label pair) distribution of the original data set into the different subsets.

title: High-order Time-Reversal Symmetry Breaking Normal State
creator: Meng Zeng, Lun-Hui Hu, Hong-Ye Hu, Yi-Zhuang You, Congjun Wu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Meng Zeng, Lun-Hui Hu, Hong-Ye Hu, Yi-Zhuang You, Congjun Wu. Spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking plays an important role in studying strongly correlated unconventional superconductors. When two superconducting gap functions with different symmetries compete, the relative phase channel ( θ − ≡ θ 1 − θ 2 \theta_{-}\equiv\theta_{1}-\theta_{2} ) exhibits an Ising-type Z 2 Z_{2} symmetry due to the second order Josephson coupling, where θ 1 , 2 \theta_{1,2} are the phases of two gap functions respectively.

title: Equidistant quenches in few-level quantum systems
creator: Sreekanth K Manikandan
description: Abstract A recent work [Phys. Rev. Lett. 125, 110602] showed that among a pair of thermodynamically equidistant quenches from a colder and a hotter initial state at a fixed ambient temperature, the relaxation from the colder initial state ( uphill relaxation) is always faster, for dynamics close to stable minima.

title: Machine-learning interatomic potentials for materials science
creator: Y. Mishin Department of Physics and Astronomy, MSN 3F3, George Mason University, Fairfax, Virginia 22030, USA
description: Abstract Large-scale atomistic computer simulations of materials rely on interatomic potentials providing computationally efficient predictions of energy and Newtonian forces. Traditional potentials have served in this capacity for over three decades. Recently, a new class of potentials has emerged, which is based on a radically different philosophy.

title: The effective model structure and ∞ \infty -groupoid objects Thanks: This version of the paper reflects the one published in Forum of Mathematics, Sigma (2022), Vol. 10:e34 1–59, submitted 9 March 2021, revised 19 January 2022, accepted 7 February 2022, available here . Two additional minor typos ha
creator: Nicola Gambino, Simon Henry, Christian Sattler, Karol Szumiło
description: Abstract For a category ℰ \mathcal{E} with finite limits and well-behaved countable coproducts, we construct a model structure, called the effective model structure, on the category of simplicial objects in ℰ \mathcal{E} , generalising the Kan–Quillen model structure on simplicial sets.

title: Decidability of Definability Issues in the Theory of Real Addition Volume: 188 Issue: 1
creator: Alexis Bès Univ. Paris Est Creteil, LACL, F-94010 Creteil, France bes@u-pec.fr, Christian Choffrut IRIF (UMR 8243), CNRS and Université Paris 7 Denis Diderot, France Christian.Choffrut@irif.fr
description: Abstract Given a subset of X ⊆ ℝ n X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n} we can associate with every point x ∈ ℝ n x\in\mathbb{R}^{n} a vector space V V of maximal dimension with the property that for some ball centered at x x , the subset X X coincides inside the ball with a union of lines parallel to V V .

title: Chiron: Optimizing Fault Tolerance in QoS-aware Distributed Stream Processing Jobs
creator: Morgan K. Geldenhuys, Lauritz Thamsen, and Odej Kao
description: Abstract Fault tolerance is a property which needs deeper consideration when dealing with streaming jobs requiring high levels of availability and low-latency processing even in case of failures where Quality-of-Service constraints must be adhered to. Typically, systems achieve fault tolerance and the ability to recover automatically from partial failures by implementing Checkpoint and Rollback Recovery.

title: COVID-19 identification from volumetric chest CT scans using a progressively resized 3D-CNN incorporating segmentation, augmentation, and class-rebalancing Journal: Artificial intelligence in medicine
creator: Md. Kamrul Hasan, Md. Tasnim Jawad, Kazi Nasim Imtiaz Hasan, Sajal Basak Partha, Md. Masum Al Masba, Shumit Saha
description: Abstract The novel COVID-19 is a global pandemic disease overgrowing worldwide. Computer-aided screening tools with greater sensitivity is imperative for disease diagnosis and prognosis as early as possible. It also can be a helpful tool in triage for testing and clinical supervision of COVID-19 patients.

title: Time-dependent Orbital-free Density Functional Theory: Background and Pauli kernel approximations
creator: Kaili Jiang, Michele Pavanello
description: Abstract Time-dependent orbital-free DFT is an efficient method for calculating the dynamic properties of large scale quantum systems due to the low computational cost compared to standard time-dependent DFT. We formalize this method by mapping the real system of interacting fermions onto a fictitious system of non-interacting bosons.

title: Zeoco: An insight into daily carbon footprint consumption
creator: Karthik Ramakrishnan, Gokul P, Preet Batavia, Shreesh Tripathi
description: Abstract . Climate change, which is now considered one of the biggest threats to humanity, is also the reason behind various other environmental concerns. Continued negligence might lead us to an irreparably damaged environment ( Solomon et al. 2009 ) .
