title: Comparative visualization of epidemiological data during various stages of a pandemic
creator: Thomas Kreuz
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Thomas Kreuz. After COVID-19 was first reported in China at the end of 2019, it took only a few months for this local crisis to turn into a global pandemic with unprecedented disruptions of everyday life. However, at any moment in time the situation in different parts of the world is far from uniform and each country follows its own epidemiological trajectory.

title: AT 2019qyl in NGC 300: Internal Collisions in the Early Outflow from a Very Fast Nova in a Symbiotic Binary This paper includes data gathered with the 6.5 m Magellan Telescopes located at Las Campanas Observatory, Chile. Based on observations made with the NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope , obtained
creator: Jacob E. Jencson, Jennifer E. Andrews, Howard E. Bond, Viraj Karambelkar, David J. Sand, Schuyler D. van Dyk, Nadejda Blagorodnova, Martha L. Boyer, Mansi M. Kasliwal, Ryan M. Lau, Shazrene Mohamed, Robert Williams, Patricia A. Whitelock, Rachael C. Amaro, K. Azalee Bostroem, Yize Dong, Michael J. L
description: Abstract Nova eruptions, thermonuclear explosions on the surfaces of white dwarfs (WDs), are now recognized to be among the most common shock-powered astrophysical transients. We present the early discovery and rapid ultraviolet (UV), optical, and infrared (IR) temporal development of AT 2019qyl, a recent nova in the nearby Sculptor Group galaxy NGC 300.

title: The effect of environment on AGN activity: the properties of radio and optical AGN in void, isolated and group galaxies Note: Not to appear in Nonlearned J., 45.
creator: Halime Miraghaei
description: Abstract The evolution of galaxies depends on their environments. In this work, active galactic nucleus (AGN) activity in different environments has been studied. The fractions of radio and optical AGN in four different environments have been compared using samples of void, isolated, group member, and the brightest group galaxies (BGGs).

title: Limit points and additive group actions Thanks: The research was supported by Russian Science Foundation, grant 19-11-00056
creator: Ivan Arzhantsev
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ivan Arzhantsev. We show that an effective action of the one-dimensional torus 𝔾 m {\mathbb{G}}_{m} on a normal affine algebraic variety X X can be extended to an effective action of a semi-direct product 𝔾 m ⋌ 𝔾 a {\mathbb{G}}_{m}\rightthreetimes{\mathbb{G}}_{a} with the same general orbit closures if and only if there is a divisor D D on X X that consists of 𝔾 m {\mathbb{G}}_{m} -fixed points.

title: Neural Feature Selection for Learning to Rank
creator: Alberto Purpura, Karolina Buchner, Gianmaria Silvello, Gian Antonio Susto
description: Abstract LEarning TO Rank (LETOR) is a research area in the field of Information Retrieval (IR) where machine learning models are employed to rank a set of items. In the past few years, neural LETOR approaches have become a competitive alternative to traditional ones like LambdaMART. However, neural architectures performance grew proportionally to their complexity and size.

title: Deconfinement Phase Transition in the S ​ U ​ ( 3 ) SU(3) Instanton-dyon Ensemble
creator: Dallas DeMartini and Edward Shuryak
description: Abstract Confinement remains one the most interesting and challenging nonperturbative phenomenon in non-Abelian gauge theories. Recent semiclassical (for SU(2)) and lattice (for QCD) studies have suggested that confinement arises from interactions of statistical ensembles of instanton-dyons with the Polyakov loop.

title: Bayesian Non-parametric Quantile Process Regression and Estimation of Marginal Quantile Effects
description: Abstract Flexible estimation of multiple conditional quantiles is of interest in numerous applications, such as studying the effect of pregnancy-related factors on low and high birth weight. We propose a Bayesian non-parametric method to simultaneously estimate non-crossing, non-linear quantile curves.

title: Fractional Korn’s inequality on subsets of the Euclidean space Thanks: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification . 26D10, 46E35, 46E40. Key words and phrases . Korn’s inequality, fractional Sobolev spaces.
creator: Artur Rutkowski
description: Abstract . We give a new, simpler proof of the fractional Korn’s inequality for subsets of ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} . We also show a framework for obtaining Korn’s inequality directly from the appropriate Hardy-type inequality. 1. Introduction Let D be a bounded open subset of \mathbb{R}^{d} , d>1 , and let p\in(1,\infty) .

title: Sharp Inference on Selected Subgroups in Observational Studies
creator: Xinzhou Guo, Linqing Wei, Chong Wu, Jingshen Wang
description: Abstract In modern drug development, the broader availability of high-dimensional observational data provides opportunities for scientist to explore subgroup heterogeneity, especially when randomized clinical trials are unavailable due to cost and ethical constraints. However, a common practice that naively searches the subgroup with a high treatment level is often misleading due to the “subgroup selection bias.

title: Bose-Einstein Condensation with Optimal Rate for Trapped Bosons in the Gross-Pitaevskii Regime
creator: Christian Brennecke, Benjamin Schlein, Severin SchravenDepartment of Mathematics, Harvard University, One Oxford Street, Cambridge MA 02138, USAInstitute of Mathematics, University of Zurich, Winterthurerstrasse 190, 8057 Zurich, Switzerland
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Christian Brennecke, Benjamin Schlein, Severin SchravenDepartment of Mathematics, Harvard University, One Oxford Street, Cambridge MA 02138, USAInstitute of Mathematics, University of Zurich, Winterthurerstrasse 190, 8057 Zurich, Switzerland. We consider a Bose gas consisting of N N particles in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} , trapped by an external field and interacting through a two-body potential with scattering length of order N − 1 N^{-1} .

title: Determining the jet transport coefficient q ^ \hat{q} from inclusive hadron suppression measurements using Bayesian parameter estimation
creator: S. Cao, Y. Chen, J. Coleman, J. Mulligan, P. M. Jacobs, R. A. Soltz, A. Angerami, R. Arora, S. A. Bass, L. Cunqueiro, T. Dai, L. Du, R. Ehlers, H. Elfner, D. Everett, W. Fan, R. J. Fries, C. Gale, F. Garza, Y. He, M. Heffernan, U. Heinz, B. V. Jacak, S. Jeon, W. Ke, B. Kim, M. Kordell II, A. Kumar,
description: Abstract We report a new determination of q ^ \hat{q} , the jet transport coefficient of the Quark-Gluon Plasma. We use the JETSCAPE framework, which incorporates a novel multi-stage theoretical approach to in-medium jet evolution and Bayesian inference for parameter extraction.

title: An ontological analysis of misinformation in online social networks
creator: Izzat Alsmadi, Iyad Alazzam, Mohammad A. Al-Ramahi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Izzat Alsmadi, Iyad Alazzam, Mohammad A. Al-Ramahi. The internet, Online Social Networks (OSNs) and smart phones enable users to create tremendous amount of information. Users who search for general or specific knowledge may not have these days problems of information scarce but misinformation. Misinformation nowadays can refer to a continuous spectrum between what can be seen as "facts" or "truth", if humans agree on the existence of such, to false information that everyone agree that it is false.

title: Suppression of spinodal instability by disorder in an athermal system Preprint: Physical Review B 104 , 144102 (2021)
creator: Tapas Bar, Arup Ghosh, Anurag Banerjee
description: Abstract We observed asymmetric critical slowing down and asymmetric dynamical scaling exponent in the superheating and supercooling kinetic processes during the thermally-induced metal-insulator transition of MnNiSn based heusler alloy. During the transition to the insulator phase, the critical-like features get enhanced compared to the transition back to the metal phase.

title: Microscopic derivation of Dirac composite fermion theory: Aspects of noncommutativity and pairing instabilities
creator: Dragoljub Gočanin, Sonja Predin, Marija Dimitrijević Ćirić, Voja Radovanović, Milica Milovanović
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Dragoljub Gočanin, Sonja Predin, Marija Dimitrijević Ćirić, Voja Radovanović, Milica Milovanović. Building on previous work [N. Senthil, 16262 (1998); Phys. B 102 , 205126 (2020)] on the system of bosons at filling factor ν = 1 \nu=1 , we derive the Dirac composite fermion theory for a half-filled Landau level from first principles and applying the Hartree-Fock approach in a preferred representation.

title: A novel mechanism for probing the Planck scale
creator: Saurya Das, Sujoy K. Modak
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Saurya Das, Sujoy K. Modak. The Planck or the quantum gravity scale, being 16 16 orders of magnitude greater than the electroweak scale, is often considered inaccessible by current experimental techniques. However, it was shown recently by one of the current authors that quantum gravity effects via the Generalized Uncertainty Principle affects the time required for free wavepackets to double their size, and this difference in time is at or near current experimental accuracies carlos1 ; carlos2 .

title: Near-Optimal Two-Pass Streaming Algorithm for Sampling Random Walks over Directed Graphs
creator: Lijie Chen, Gillat Kol, Dmitry Paramonov, Raghuvansh R. Saxena, Zhao Song, Huacheng Yu
description: Abstract For a directed graph G G with n n vertices and a start vertex u 𝗌𝗍𝖺𝗋𝗍 u_{\sf start} , we wish to (approximately) sample an L L -step random walk over G G starting from u 𝗌𝗍𝖺𝗋𝗍 u_{\sf start} with minimum space using an algorithm that only makes few passes over the edges of the graph.

title: Generative Archimedean Copulas
creator: Yuting Ng, Ali Hasan, Khalil Elkhalil, Vahid Tarokh
description: Abstract We propose a new generative modeling technique for learning multidimensional cumulative distribution functions (CDFs) in the form of copulas. Specifically, we consider certain classes of copulas known as Archimedean and hierarchical Archimedean copulas, popular for their parsimonious representation and ability to model different tail dependencies.

title: Supersymmetric domain walls in maximal 6D gauged supergravity I
description: Abstract We find a large class of supersymmetric domain wall solutions from six-dimensional N = ( 2 , 2 ) N=(2,2) gauged supergravity with various gauge groups. In general, the embedding tensor lives in 𝟏𝟒𝟒 c \mathbf{144}_{c} representation of the global symmetry S ​ O ​ ( 5 , 5 ) SO(5,5) .

title: A supra-massive population of stellar-mass black holes in the globular cluster Palomar 5
creator: M. Gieles 1,2, D. Erkal 3, F. Antonini 4, Eduardo Balbinot 5 and Jorge Peñarrubia 6,7
description: Abstract Palomar 5 is one of the sparsest star clusters in the Galactic halo and is best-known for its spectacular tidal tails, spanning over 20 degrees across the sky. With N N -body simulations we show that both distinguishing features can result from a stellar-mass black hole population, comprising ∼ 20 % \sim 20\% of the present-day cluster mass.

title: Wave Function Collapse, Correlating Interactions, and Conservation Laws
creator: Edward J. Gillis
description: Abstract The assumption that wave function collapse is induced by correlating interactions of the kind that constitute measurements leads to a stochastic collapse equation that does not require the introduction of any new physical constants and that is consistent with conservation laws.

title: MixUp Training Leads to Reduced Overfitting and Improved Calibration for the Transformer Architecture
creator: Wancong Zhang, Ieshan Vaidya
description: Abstract MixUp is a computer vision data augmentation technique that uses convex interpolations of input data and their labels to enhance model generalization during training. However, the application of MixUp to the natural language understanding (NLU) domain has been limited, due to the difficulty of interpolating text directly in the input space.

title: Higher-order topological phases in tunable C 3 C_{3} -symmetric photonic crystals
creator: Hai-Xiao Wang, Li Liang, Bin Jiang, Junhui Hu, Xiancong Lu, Jian-Hua Jiang
description: Abstract We demonstrate that multiple higher-order topological transitions can be triggered via the continuous change of the geometry in kagome photonic crystals composed of three dielectric rods. By tuning a single geometry parameter, the photonic corner and edge states emerge or disappear with the higher-order topological transitions. Two distinct higher-order topological insulator phases and a normal insulator phase are revealed.

title: Heisenberg-limited ground state energy estimation for early fault-tolerant quantum computers
creator: Lin Lin, Yu Tong
description: Abstract Under suitable assumptions, the quantum phase estimation (QPE) algorithm is able to achieve Heisenberg-limited precision scaling in estimating the ground state energy. However, QPE requires a large number of ancilla qubits and large circuit depth, as well as the ability to perform inverse quantum Fourier transform, making it expensive to implement on an early fault-tolerant quantum computer.

title: β \beta -Delayed Neutron and Fission Calculations with Relativistic QRPA and Statistical Model
creator: Futoshi Minato, Tomislav Marketin, Nils Paar
description: Abstract Background: A role of β \beta -delayed neutron emission and fission in r r -process nucleosynthesis attracts a high interest. Although the number of study on them covering r r -process nuclei is increasing recently, uncertainties of β \beta -delayed neutron and fission are still large for r r -process simulations.

title: Quantitative analysis of non-equilibrium systems from short-time experimental data
creator: Sreekanth K Manikandan 1, 4, Subhrokoli Ghosh 2, 4, Avijit Kundu 2, Biswajit Das 2, Vipin Agrawal 1, 3, Dhrubaditya Mitra 1, 3, Ayan Banerjee 2, Supriya Krishnamurthy 3
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sreekanth K Manikandan 1, 4, Subhrokoli Ghosh 2, 4, Avijit Kundu 2, Biswajit Das 2, Vipin Agrawal 1, 3, Dhrubaditya Mitra 1, 3, Ayan Banerjee 2, Supriya Krishnamurthy 3. We provide a minimal strategy for the quantitative analysis of a large class of non-equilibrium systems in a statistically steady state using the short-time Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation (TUR).

title: Reinforcement Learning of Beam Codebooks in Millimeter Wave and Terahertz MIMO Systems
creator: Yu Zhang, Muhammad Alrabeiah, Ahmed Alkhateeb
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yu Zhang, Muhammad Alrabeiah, Ahmed Alkhateeb. Millimeter wave (mmWave) and terahertz MIMO systems rely on pre-defined beamforming codebooks for both initial access and data transmission. Being pre-defined, however, those codebooks are commonly not optimized for specific environments, user distributions, and/or possible hardware impairments. This leads to large codebook sizes with high beam training overhead which increases the initial access/tracking latency and makes it hard for these systems to support highly mobile applications.

title: Signatures of elastoviscous buckling in the dilute rheology of stiff polymers
creator: Brato Chakrabarti, Yanan Liu, Olivia du Roure, Anke Lindner, David Saintillan
description: Abstract As a stiff polymer tumbles in shear flow, it experiences compressive viscous forces that can cause it to buckle and undergo a sequence of morphological transitions with increasing flow strength. We use numerical simulations to uncover the effects of these transitions on the steady shear rheology of a dilute suspension of stiff polymers.
